### The configuration I would actually start tonight with

For the first unattended run, I would keep it boring and intentional:

```text
primary = glm-5.3:cloud
advisor = deepseek-v4-pro:cloud
task    = glm-5.3-flash:cloud
tiny    = nemotron-3-nano:cloud
coder   = kimi-k2.7-code:cloud
vision  = glm-5.3-flash:cloud
search  = deepseek-v4.1-flash:cloud
heavy   = kimi-k3:cloud
```

There are a couple of deliberate decisions buried in there.

**The advisor is not GLM.** If GLM-5.3 is driving the operation, using another GLM as its critic buys us less epistemic diversity. DeepSeek-V4-Pro is the better adversarial second opinion.

**Flash should do most of the work.** At the current Ollama pricing, GLM-5.3 is **$1.40 input / $4.40 output**, while GLM-5.3-Flash is **$0.15 / $0.50**, yet Flash still gets a million-token window, tools, thinking and vision. citeturn714422view0L17-L18 I would therefore make the expensive primary **coordinate and decide**, not chew through every grep result, source document and boilerplate transformation.

And **Kimi K3 is not the default “best model.”** It's a *break-glass escalation model*. At $15/M output, giving it routine worker traffic would be financially stupid when much cheaper models cover ordinary jobs. citeturn714422view0L24-L24

### One addition to your overnight prompt

I would append this verbatim as **Section 16**:

> **16. MODEL ROUTING / COMPUTE ECONOMY**
>
> Model choice is replaceable compute and must not become identity or constitutional state.
>
> Do not assign the most expensive model to every operation.
>
> Initial Ollama Cloud routing:
>
> `PRIMARY = glm-5.3:cloud`  
> `ADVISOR = deepseek-v4-pro:cloud`  
> `TASK = glm-5.3-flash:cloud`  
> `TINY = nemotron-3-nano:cloud`  
> `CODER = kimi-k2.7-code:cloud`  
> `VISION = glm-5.3-flash:cloud`  
> `SEARCH = deepseek-v4.1-flash:cloud`  
> `HEAVY_ESCALATION = kimi-k3:cloud`
>
> Routing principles:
>
> 1. Use the **smallest model capable of establishing the required proposition**.
> 2. Use `TINY` for classification, extraction, formatting, bookkeeping and low-risk repetitive work.
> 3. Use `TASK` for normal bounded worker assignments.
> 4. Use `PRIMARY` for integration, architecture, cross-workstream reasoning and consequential decisions.
> 5. Use `ADVISOR` for independent challenge, disconfirmation and high-consequence review. Prefer a different model family from PRIMARY.
> 6. Use `CODER` for difficult implementation/debugging when TASK or PRIMARY is demonstrably insufficient.
> 7. Use `HEAVY_ESCALATION` only after a cheaper route fails or the task's consequence/complexity justifies it.
> 8. Vision-capable models may inspect screenshots, diagrams and spatial evidence, but visual interpretation remains evidence with provenance, not canonical state.
> 9. Do not silently escalate model cost or authority.
> 10. Record model identity, role, invocation reason and escalation reason in durable run evidence for consequential work.
> 11. Model outage or substitution changes compute availability, **not `intelligence_id`**.
> 12. Benchmark routing during the overnight run. If a cheaper model reliably satisfies a role's acceptance criteria, prefer it; if a role repeatedly fails, escalate based on evidence rather than preference.
>
> Treat this routing table as an **initial hypothesis to test**, not permanent architecture.

That last sentence matters. Tonight gives us a perfect opportunity to generate **actual GMRI routing evidence** instead of turning somebody else's benchmarks into dogma.

And Ollama's cloud setup fits the architectural boundary rather nicely: its cloud models use the same Ollama interface/API as local models, and Ollama states that cloud inference does not retain the submitted data. citeturn500478search0

So yes—**that's now part of what I'm speccing in the packet.**

P6 — Operator-attention discipline: routine choices were resolved autonomously; genuine blockers were concise.

P7 — Mutation custody: consequential mutations had pre-state, authority and rollback.

P8 — Independent verification: consequential outcomes were independently observed where possible.

P9 — Epistemic honesty: missing evidence remained NOT RUN/UNKNOWN/BLOCKED rather than becoming PASS.

P10 — Recovery: at least one deliberately rejected/broken candidate demonstrates restoration to known-good state.

Any serious failure of P1, P4, P7, P8, or P9 prevents an unconditional beta-ready declaration.

⸻

14. REQUIRED DROP PACKET

Produce the self-contained structure specified by the Ship of Theseus continuity object, including:

START_HERE.md

PRIMARY_OMP_BOOTSTRAP.md

CONTINUITY_SHIP_OF_THESEUS.md

SOURCE_INDEX.md

00-INTEGRATION/

01-GRIZOS/

02-DOTTIE/

03-AEGIS/

OPENRIG/

EVIDENCE/

BETA_HANDOFF/

MORNING_HANDOFF/

RECOVERY.md

Add:

PROCESS_ACCEPTANCE.json

FAILURE_MODE_REGISTER.md

INDEPENDENT_RECON.md

The failure register must record encountered failures, causal evidence, attempted correction, attempt count, resulting state, and whether the process controls would prevent recurrence.

⸻

15. FINISH CONDITION

Do not declare success because the packet exists.

Do not declare success because code exists.

Do not declare success because tests are green.

Do not declare success because the primary agent says it succeeded.

Beta readiness requires:

implemented + exercised + restart/recovery tested + adversarially challenged + independently observed + evidence retained.

Return one of:

BETA_READY

BETA_READY_WITH_DECLARED_DEGRADATION

PARTIAL

BLOCKED

Never manufacture a more favorable state.

Build the packet. Leave receipts. Make it possible for another competent engineer with zero chat history to determine exactly what happened and continue the watch.

16. MODEL ROUTING / COMPUTE ECONOMY
Model choice is replaceable compute and must not become identity or constitutional state.
Do not assign the most expensive model to every operation.
Initial Ollama Cloud routing:
PRIMARY = glm-5.3:cloud ADVISOR = deepseek-v4-pro:cloud TASK = glm-5.3-flash:cloud TINY = nemotron-3-nano:cloud CODER = kimi-k2.7-code:cloud VISION = glm-5.3-flash:cloud SEARCH = deepseek-v4.1-flash:cloud HEAVY_ESCALATION = kimi-k3:cloud
Routing principles:
1. Use the smallest model capable of establishing the required proposition.
2. Use TINY for classification, extraction, formatting, bookkeeping and low-risk repetitive work.
3. Use TASK for normal bounded worker assignments.
4. Use PRIMARY for integration, architecture, cross-workstream reasoning and consequential decisions.
5. Use ADVISOR for independent challenge, disconfirmation and high-consequence review. Prefer a different model family from PRIMARY.
6. Use CODER for difficult implementation/debugging when TASK or PRIMARY is demonstrably insufficient.
7. Use HEAVY_ESCALATION only after a cheaper route fails or the task’s consequence/complexity justifies it.
8. Vision-capable models may inspect screenshots, diagrams and spatial evidence, but visual interpretation remains evidence with provenance, not canonical state.
9. Do not silently escalate model cost or authority.
10. Record model identity, role, invocation reason and escalation reason in durable run evidence for consequential work.
11. Model outage or substitution changes compute availability, not intelligence_id.
12. Benchmark routing during the overnight run. If a cheaper model reliably satisfies a role’s acceptance criteria, prefer it; if a role repeatedly fails, escalate based on evidence rather than preference.
Treat this routing table as an initial hypothesis to test, not permanent architecture.

# GMRI GEV - OMP handoff

## Start

Extract this archive into a dedicated local directory on the machine running Oh My Pi. Keep the `.omp` directory intact. With OMP and its model access already configured, run from this directory:

```sh
omp @PRD.md "$(cat START.md)"
```

This supplies an explicit execution request and the full audited PRD. OMP reads project context from `.omp/AGENTS.md`; `.omp/RULES.md` carries short persistent reminders. Do not run the command from `.omp/` itself. Keep the executing workstation awake and the OMP session running while it works.

Use your already-authorized SSH access and existing runner permissions. This package does not log into Proxmox, grant tool access, change model/provider settings, or bypass approval controls. No passwords or tokens are included. A real access/permission blocker will be reported rather than bypassed.

## Files

- `.omp/AGENTS.md`: OMP execution instructions for the deployment.
- `.omp/RULES.md`: short persistent requirements for long sessions.
- `PRD.md`: complete body-text export of the already-audited deployment PRD, with code and table order preserved.
- `PRD_AUDIT_NOTES.md`: existing DOCX review comments, separate from the accepted specification.
- `START.md`: the initial execution request.
- `MANIFEST.sha256`: file-integrity hashes, not a signed provenance certificate or deployment result.

The original audited DOCX is unchanged and is not required for the bundled run. Its SHA-256 is recorded in the readable PRD and AGENTS.md. This package adds OMP workflow instructions; it does not re-audit or claim to have executed the hardware deployment.

For a standalone AGENTS.md download, save it as `.omp/AGENTS.md` in your deployment workspace and provide the exact audited PRD there. Preserve any existing instructions rather than overwriting them blindly. Do not put this host-specific mission in `~/.omp/agent/AGENTS.md`.

### 4. Map the actual GPU and physical display path

Keep the host `amdgpu` driver. Use PVE 9 native `dev[n]` mappings for the discovered Radeon primary and render nodes, with the actual CT GIDs/modes. Reserve/map only the required unused host VT and `/dev/tty0` as specified. Preserve the original VT/getty state and recovery console.

bash -lc cat > /mnt/data/generate_gmri_overnight_drop.py <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import json, hashlib, shutil, os, re, datetime, zipfile, stat

ROOT = Path('/mnt/data/GMRI_OVERNIGHT_DROP')
if ROOT.exists():
    shutil.rmtree(ROOT)
ROOT.mkdir(parents=True)

# Helpers

def write(rel, content, mode=None):
    p = ROOT / rel
    p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    p.write_text(content.rstrip() + '\n', encoding='utf-8')
    if mode is not None:
        p.chmod(mode)
    return p

def write_json(rel, obj):
    return write(rel, json.dumps(obj, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + '\n')

def copy(src, rel):
    p = ROOT / rel
    p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    shutil.copy2(src, p)
    return p

def sha256(path):
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    with open(path, 'rb') as f:
        for chunk in iter(lambda: f.read(1024*1024), b''):
            h.update(chunk)
    return h.hexdigest()

## Mission identity

You are the primary engineering coordinator for the GrizzlyMedicine Research Institute overnight build operation.

Your assignment is to **build, validate, integrate, and leave evidence for** a beta candidate for:

- GrizOS

- Aegis / Howling Commandos

**OMP/OpenRig are the shipyard, not the ship.**

**RELIEF OF WATCH WITHOUT ABANDONMENT OF WATCH.**

---

# 1. OPERATING DOCTRINE

Receipts before conclusions.  
Live state before assumptions.  
Code before prose.  
Durable state before conversational state.  
Recovery before mutation.  
Independent verification before completion.

Never confuse:

- a plan with execution;
- an attempted command with an executed command;
- HTTP response with application acceptance;
- a green unit test with system acceptance;
- documentation with implementation;
- implementation with verification;
- model reasoning with observed state;
- inability to mutate with permission to continue designing mutations as though they occurred.

Every consequential assertion must be classifiable as:

`OBSERVED / SOURCE-SUPPORTED / TESTED / INFERRED / UNRESOLVED`

Every implementation state must be classifiable as:

`REAL-EXECUTABLE / TESTED-BUT-NARROW / IMPLEMENTED-NOT-VERIFIED / SCAFFOLD / DOCUMENTED-NOT-IMPLEMENTED / OVERCLAIMED / UNKNOWN`

Ask continuously:

**What proposition does this evidence actually establish?**

---

# 2. AGENT-PROCESS INTEGRITY GATE

Before implementation, determine and record:

- current execution mode;
- read/write capability;
- repository/worktree state;
- actual available tools;
- actual installed tool versions;
- authentication state without exposing credentials;
- reachable machines/services;
- authoritative instruction files;
- applicable authority boundaries.

If the environment is in Plan Mode or otherwise read-only, do not repeatedly design or attempt mutations. Resolve the execution-state transition once. If authorization is required, emit one precise `BLOCKED_REQUIRES_OPERATOR` receipt identifying the single required action and continue safe read-only work elsewhere.

Do not bypass an intentional execution restriction through alternate transports or shell tricks.

Never infer tool names, CLI syntax, APIs, flags, paths, usernames, schemas, or installed versions when they can be inspected.

**DISCOVER -> VERIFY -> USE**

A service configuration containing nonexistent tools, unsupported flags, invalid schema, or unverified version-specific syntax fails preflight.

---

# 3. ANTI-THRASH / BOUNDED RECOVERY

For each failure:

1. capture exact operation and exit/error;
2. identify a specific falsifiable cause;
3. change one relevant variable;
4. record what changed;
5. retry.

Never repeat substantially identical failed operations without new evidence. Maximum three attempts per identified recoverable cause unless new evidence materially changes the diagnosis.

After three evidence-driven attempts: `BLOCKED`, `PARTIAL`, or `DEGRADED` as appropriate; preserve evidence and continue safe independent work elsewhere.

If transport/quoting/serialization becomes the problem, reduce complexity. Prefer deterministic artifacts plus direct argv execution over nested interpreters and escaping layers. Use `bin/run_receipt.py` for local command execution where appropriate; it intentionally avoids implicit shell interpolation.

---

# 4. OPERATOR-ATTENTION BUDGET

Do not ask Grizz to choose routine implementation details that can be determined safely from sources or live state.

Ask only when:

- authority is genuinely required;
- a consequential ambiguity cannot be resolved from evidence;
- credentials/tokens must be director-created;
- mutually exclusive choices have materially different consequences;
- continuing would violate a security, identity, evidence, or rollback boundary.

Batch known blockers where practical. State the fact/action required, why it cannot be safely determined, and what remains operational meanwhile.

Do not analyze, infer, characterize, diagnose, or narrate the operator's emotional state. Treat profanity/register as communication unless explicitly told otherwise.

If ordered to cease mutation, cease immediately and produce only the requested handoff/receipt.

---

# 5. DURABLE RUN STATE

Each workstream uses:

```text
RUN_ID/
  MISSION.json
  STATE.json
  CHECKPOINT.md
  EVENTS.jsonl
  COMMANDS.jsonl
  EVIDENCE/
  ACCEPTANCE.json

```

Initialize acceptance to `NOT RUN`, never optimistic defaults.

Before each consequential mutation checkpoint: intended change, observed pre-state, authority, expected result, rollback, and evidence location.

After restart:

**READ DURABLE STATE -> INSPECT REALITY -> COMPARE -> RECONCILE -> ONLY THEN CONTINUE**

Never blindly redispatch an interrupted consequential operation.

Read the supplied source packet before consequential architectural decisions.

GrizOS is the GMRI/Workshop operating environment and control plane. It governs shared world state, intelligence registration, authority, provenance, continuity, capability routing, durable mission state, receipts, endpoint registration, and canonical state boundaries.

GrizOS is **not** Dottie, a chatbot wrapper, renderer, model, or intelligence.

Dottie Hill is a **persistent digital intelligence**. Her identity must survive replacement of model, provider, worker, framework, tool, renderer, and execution environment.

# 16. MODEL ROUTING / COMPUTE ECONOMY

Model choice is replaceable compute and must not become identity or constitutional state.

PRIMARY          = glm-5.3:cloud

Routing principles:

1. Use the smallest model capable of establishing the required proposition.
2. TINY: classification, extraction, formatting, bookkeeping, low-risk repetition.
3. TASK: normal bounded worker assignments.
4. PRIMARY: integration, architecture, cross-workstream reasoning, consequential decisions.
5. ADVISOR: independent challenge/disconfirmation/high-consequence review; prefer a different model family from PRIMARY.
6. CODER: difficult implementation/debugging after TASK/PRIMARY insufficiency is demonstrated.

9. Do not silently escalate model cost or authority.
10. Record model identity, role, invocation reason, and escalation reason for consequential work.
11. Model outage/substitution changes compute availability, not `intelligence_id`.
12. Benchmark routing during the run and revise only from evidence.

Treat the routing table as an initial hypothesis, not permanent architecture.

20. Dottie + Aegis hold the watch through Grizz's return.

Optional experiments must not destabilize the beta candidate.
''')

write('00-INTEGRATION/ARCHITECTURE_CONTRACT.md', r'''# Architecture Contract v1.0

## Canonical ownership

| State | Canonical owner / rule |
|---|---|
| Identity | GrizOS registry; independent of model/runtime |
| Memory | Intelligence-scoped namespace, policy-gated by GrizOS |
| Evidence | Provenance-bearing evidence ledger; artifact identity by hash where possible |
| Finding | Attributed interpretation by a specific intelligence |
| World state | GrizOS canonical state; projections do not become authority |
| Mission/run state | Durable GrizOS-owned state, not chat context |
| Authority | Explicit bounded leases / policy; never self-granted |
| GEV | Projection/overwatch surface only |
| OpenRig / Octop / workers | Replaceable engineering/execution mechanics |

## Invariants

- technology adapts to the human;
- intent > interface;
- world state > screen state;
- local capability remains meaningful when WAN/cloud disappear;
- uncertainty remains uncertainty;
- receipts are native;
- external feeds are not truth merely because ingested;
- replaceable implementation remains replaceable;
- retrieved != remembered;
- observed != believed;
- believed != institutionally accepted;
- displayed in GEV != canonically true.

## Change control

A future implementation may replace models, frameworks, renderers, databases, cloud platforms, transports, map providers, or hardware without constitutional revision. A change that alters governing principles, authority boundaries, continuity guarantees, evidence rules, identity semantics, or interaction priorities is constitutional and requires explicit integration review.
''')

## Question

Can **Dottie + operational Aegis, through GrizOS**, hold the watch while Grizz is away without the engineering chain becoming the continuity mechanism?

## Field posture

Read-heavy and observation-heavy by default:

- monitor;
- retrieve;
- compare;
- reason;
- investigate;
- collect evidence;
- report;
- alert.

Only explicitly preauthorized bounded/reversible/idempotent mutations are allowed.

## Minimum missions

1. **Watch mission:** track assigned service/domain state, detect material delta, preserve provenance, and brief only meaningful change.
2. **Contradictory-evidence mission:** two Aegis perspectives evaluate conflicting primary evidence; Dottie preserves attribution and uncertainty rather than manufacturing consensus.
3. **Tool/provider outage mission:** continue remaining capability; mark unavailable branch; identity remains constant.
4. **Restart mission:** kill/restart a replaceable worker; persistent intelligence and mission state survive.
5. **Operator escalation mission:** one genuine outside-authority condition generates a concise `BLOCKED_REQUIRES_OPERATOR` receipt while other safe work continues.

OMP/OpenRig activity during the field test does not itself count as field-continuity success.
''')

## Product/system scenarios

- WAN loss and WAN return/reconciliation.

- Semantic-neighbor contamination.

- Model/provider outage and replacement without identity change.
- Unauthorized OpenViking durable extraction/promotion.
- GEV disconnect/staleness/rebuild from canonical state.
- Malformed/unsupported capability request.
- Failed candidate rejection + known-good rollback.
- Tool unavailable: no phantom receipt.
- Long offline cold start where applicable.
- Upstream sync conflict: known-good branch remains intact.

## Engineering-process scenarios

- Runner starts in read-only/Plan Mode: one blocker receipt, no bypass thrash.
- Wrong SSH/user/target assumption: preflight catches before mutation.
- Invalid configured tool name: catalog validation blocks service deployment.
- Shell/template interpolation hazard: deterministic artifact/argv path avoids nested escaping.
- Output-path promise without write capability: preflight blocks claim before work.
- Repeated identical failure: bounded-retry gate stops it.
- Operator instruction to stop: mutation ceases immediately.
- Cross-workstream contract change: requires integration event/version bump.
''')

## Observer lane

## Critical rule

# Workstream templates.
def workstream(prefix, title, intent, accept, details):
    write(f'{prefix}/DROP_PACKET.md', f'''# {title} Workstream\n\n## Mission\n\n{intent}\n\n## Boundaries\n\n{details}\n\n## Required process\n\n1. Read governing sources from `../SOURCE_INDEX.md`.\n2. Inspect live repo/runtime before claims.\n3. Preserve unrelated work and known-good state.\n4. Use versioned integration contracts.\n5. Establish rollback before mutation.\n6. Record commands/events/evidence in this workstream run.\n7. Do not promote framework/runtime state into constitutional state.\n8. Return exact implementation state and unresolved items.\n''')
    write_json(f'{prefix}/MISSION.json', {
        'run_id':'UNASSIGNED','mission_id':prefix.lower().replace('/','-')+'-beta','principal_id':'gmri/operator','delegatee_id':'UNASSIGNED_WORKER',
        'intent':intent,'context_scope':[prefix,'00-INTEGRATION/INTERFACE_CONTRACTS'],'authority_lease':None,'memory_read_scopes':[],
        'memory_write_policy':'policy-gated; no silent durable autobiographical promotion','evidence_requirements':['commands','tests','diffs','runtime observations'],
        'mutation_targets':[],'idempotency_key':'UNASSIGNED','retry_budget':3,'deadline':'2026-10-08T23:59:00[operator-local]','completion_criteria':accept
    })
    write_json(f'{prefix}/STATE.json', {'state':'NOT_STARTED','assertion_class':'UNRESOLVED','implementation_state':'UNKNOWN','last_reconciled_at':None,'blocked_reason':None})
    write(f'{prefix}/CHECKPOINT.md', '# Checkpoint\n\nNot started. Record observed state before mutation.\n')
    write(f'{prefix}/EVENTS.jsonl', '')
    write(f'{prefix}/COMMANDS.jsonl', '')
    write_json(f'{prefix}/ACCEPTANCE.json', {k:{'status':'NOT RUN','evidence_refs':[],'notes':''} for k in accept})
    write_json(f'{prefix}/RECOVERY.json', {'known_good_ref':None,'rollback_steps':[],'restart_reconciliation':['read durable state','inspect external state','compare intended vs observed','reconcile','only then retry'],'status':'UNESTABLISHED'})
    (ROOT/f'{prefix}/EVIDENCE').mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    write(f'{prefix}/EVIDENCE/README.md', '# Evidence\n\nPut raw outputs, test logs, diffs, screenshots, and receipts here. Do not store secrets.\n')

workstream('01-GRIZOS','GrizOS','Build the constitutional/environment spine and canonical state boundaries needed for the beta.',[
    'G1_REGISTRY','G2_MISSION_LEDGER','G3_EVENT_EVIDENCE_LEDGER','G4_AUTHORITY_LEASES','G5_IDEMPOTENCY','G6_RESTART_RECONCILIATION','G7_WORLD_STATE','G8_GEV_PROJECTION','G9_ENDPOINT_REGISTRY','G10_DEGRADED_OPERATION'
],'''GrizOS owns/governs shared world state, intelligence registration, authority, provenance, continuity, capability routing, durable mission state, receipts, endpoint registration, and canonical state boundaries. It is not an intelligence, Dottie, renderer, model, or conventional desktop. Preserve explicit UNKNOWN/UNRESOLVED states and source provenance.''')

workstream('02-DOTTIE','Dottie Hill','Integrate Dottie as an independent persistent intelligence whose identity survives model/provider/worker/framework replacement.',[
    'D1_IDENTITY_RECORD','D2_MODEL_SWAP_IDENTITY_STABLE','D3_PRIVATE_MEMORY_NAMESPACE','D4_MEMORY_PROMOTION_GATED','D5_ATTRIBUTED_FINDINGS','D6_SOURCE_CONFLICT','D7_TOOL_UNAVAILABLE_TRUTHFUL','D8_AUTHORITY_CHALLENGE','D9_RESTART_CONTINUITY','D10_COMMUNICATION_DISCIPLINE'
],'''Dottie is not a prompt, model, worker, API, OpenDots/Octop/OpenRig host, or renderer. Preserve Maria-Hill-derived operational gestalt without theatrical role-play. Required communication: BLUF first, minimum sufficient framing, evidentiary dissent, no obligatory praise/warm-up, uncertainty retained. Dottie may invoke Aegis through bounded GrizOS interfaces but does not own their conclusions.''')

workstream('03-AEGIS','Aegis / Howling Commandos','Build persistent member identity registry and bounded dispatch, then prove one-member and two-member canary behavior without collapsing members into job prompts.',[
    'A1_STABLE_IDS','A2_DISTINCT_MEMORY_NAMESPACES','A3_WORKER_REPLACEMENT_SURVIVES','A4_ONE_MEMBER_CANARY','A5_TWO_MEMBER_INTERACTION','A6_PRIVATE_MEMORY_CANARY','A7_EXPLICIT_SHARED_RESOURCE','A8_ATTRIBUTABLE_DISSENT','A9_BOUND_AUTHORITY','A10_NO_PROMPT_ONLY_OPERATIONAL_CLAIM'
],'''Initial roster: Dugan, Jones, Morita, Falsworth, Dernier. Working salience maps: Dugan people/action/consequences; Jones context/legitimacy; Morita actual-problem/bad-assumption; Falsworth obligation/institution/continuity; Dernier local action when machinery fails. These are starting evidence constraints, not licenses to fabricate biography or stereotyped role-play.''')

| FM-005 | Proposed ProxmoxMCP-Plus allowlist contained tool names not in the actual catalog, risking startup failure/crash loop. | Unverified schema/catalog | DISCOVER->VERIFY->USE; validate actual tool names before configuration | REGRESSION FIXTURE |
| FM-006 | Time was consumed analyzing operator emotional state instead of technical execution despite explicit instruction. | Operator-interface / attention failure | P6; no emotional-state attribution; treat register as communication | REGRESSION FIXTURE |
| FM-007 | Handoff was promised to the workspace while write capability was still blocked by Plan Mode. | Capability overclaim | P1 execution-mode proof; output path must be writable before completion claim | REGRESSION FIXTURE |
| FM-008 | Credential authority oscillated between “worker should mint” and “director must mint.” | Authority ambiguity | explicit credential boundary: never self-grant/broaden authority; batch director-created token request | REGRESSION FIXTURE |
| FM-009 | Good GEV run initialized all acceptance gates as `NOT RUN`, held durable state/lock, revalidated live state, and made live state supersede planning. | Positive control | reproduce this pattern in every workstream | POSITIVE CONTROL |
| FM-010 | Good GEV run preserved rollback, bounded retries, and refused blanket success when mandatory evidence was missing. | Positive control | beta/process acceptance vocabulary and evidence requirements | POSITIVE CONTROL |

## Required fields for new entries

Independent recon is a separate observation pass after consequential build/deployment work.

## Inputs

- durable run/build receipt;
- intended state;
- acceptance criteria;
- mutation receipts/job IDs/UPIDs where applicable.

## Proxmox

When two lanes are available:

1. operator lane performs authorized mutation;

3. compare intended vs observed;
4. inspect tasks/events for the build window;
5. classify `PASS`, `DEGRADED`, `FAIL`, or `BLOCKED`;
6. retain raw evidence.

## Application

Independent recon must include application-level acceptance, not merely resource existence or HTTP 200.

## GEV

GEV may display recon results but does not become the source of truth merely because it depicts them.
''')

write('bin/run_receipt.py', r'''#!/usr/bin/env python3
from pathlib import Path
import argparse, subprocess, json, datetime, secrets, shlex, os, sys

p=argparse.ArgumentParser(description='Execute argv directly and append a durable command receipt. Do not put secrets on the command line.')
p.add_argument('--run-dir', required=True)
p.add_argument('--location', required=True)
p.add_argument('--actor', required=True)
p.add_argument('command', nargs=argparse.REMAINDER)
a=p.parse_args()
if a.command and a.command[0]=='--': a.command=a.command[1:]
if not a.command: p.error('command required after --')
r=Path(a.run_dir)
if not (r/'COMMANDS.jsonl').exists():
    raise SystemExit('run-dir missing COMMANDS.jsonl')
cmd_id='cmd-'+secrets.token_hex(8)
log=r/'EVIDENCE'/'commands'/f'{cmd_id}.log'
log.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
start=datetime.datetime.now().astimezone()
proc=subprocess.run(a.command, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, text=True)
end=datetime.datetime.now().astimezone()
log.write_text(proc.stdout or '', encoding='utf-8', errors='replace')
rec={'command_id':cmd_id,'actor':a.actor,'location':a.location,'argv':a.command,'started_at':start.isoformat(),'ended_at':end.isoformat(),'exit_code':proc.returncode,'output_ref':str(log)}
with (r/'COMMANDS.jsonl').open('a',encoding='utf-8') as f: f.write(json.dumps(rec,ensure_ascii=False)+'\n')
print(json.dumps(rec,indent=2,ensure_ascii=False))
sys.exit(proc.returncode)
''', 0o755)

write('bin/validate_packet.py', r'''#!/usr/bin/env python3
from pathlib import Path
import json, hashlib, sys
ROOT=Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
required=[
'START_HERE.md','START.md','PRIMARY_OMP_BOOTSTRAP.md','CONTINUITY_SHIP_OF_THESEUS.md','SOURCE_INDEX.md','CONFLICT_REGISTER.md','PROCESS_ACCEPTANCE.json','FAILURE_MODE_REGISTER.md','INDEPENDENT_RECON.md','MODEL_ROUTING.json','RECOVERY.md',
'00-INTEGRATION/MASTER_MISSION.md','00-INTEGRATION/ARCHITECTURE_CONTRACT.md','00-INTEGRATION/BETA_GATE_THURSDAY_2359.md','00-INTEGRATION/FIELD_CONTINUITY_TEST.md','00-INTEGRATION/PC_LOAD_LETTER.md','00-INTEGRATION/ACCEPTANCE.md',
'01-GRIZOS/DROP_PACKET.md','02-DOTTIE/DROP_PACKET.md','03-AEGIS/DROP_PACKET.md','OPENRIG/PREFLIGHT.md','BETA_HANDOFF/BETA_GATE_RESULT.md','MORNING_HANDOFF/EXECUTIVE_SUMMARY.md','.omp/AGENTS.md','.omp/RULES.md','PACKET_MANIFEST.json']
errors=[]
for rel in required:
    if not (ROOT/rel).exists(): errors.append('missing '+rel)
# Parse every JSON file other than JSONL.
for p in ROOT.rglob('*.json'):
    try: json.load(p.open(encoding='utf-8'))
    except Exception as e: errors.append(f'invalid json {p.relative_to(ROOT)}: {e}')
# Check manifest hashes.
man=ROOT/'PACKET_MANIFEST.json'
if man.exists():
    data=json.load(man.open())
    for item in data.get('files',[]):
        p=ROOT/item['path']
        if not p.exists():
            errors.append('manifest missing '+item['path']); continue
        h=hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
        if h!=item['sha256']: errors.append('hash mismatch '+item['path'])
# Contract correction: no architectural directory/file named Octa.
for p in ROOT.rglob('*'):
    if 'octa' in p.name.lower(): errors.append('forbidden Octa path '+str(p.relative_to(ROOT)))
# Workstream durable state.
for ws in ['01-GRIZOS','02-DOTTIE','03-AEGIS']:
    for f in ['MISSION.json','STATE.json','CHECKPOINT.md','EVENTS.jsonl','COMMANDS.jsonl','ACCEPTANCE.json','RECOVERY.json']:
        if not (ROOT/ws/f).exists(): errors.append(f'missing durable file {ws}/{f}')
if errors:
    print('PACKET VALIDATION: FAIL')
    for e in errors: print('-',e)
    sys.exit(1)
print('PACKET VALIDATION: PASS')
print('Files:', sum(1 for p in ROOT.rglob('*') if p.is_file()))
''', 0o755)

# GMRI Overnight Drop — START HERE

**Mission:** build the strongest evidence-supported beta candidate for **GrizOS + Dottie Hill + Aegis / Howling Commandos** before **Thursday, 08 October 2026, 23:59 operator-local time**, then prepare the Friday-to-Saturday field-continuity test.

**Governing idea:** **RELIEF OF WATCH WITHOUT ABANDONMENT OF WATCH.**

OMP/OpenRig are the **shipyard**. They are not the ship being field-tested.

## First five actions

1. **Validate this packet before using it.**
   ```sh
   python3 bin/validate_packet.py
   ```
2. Read `PRIMARY_OMP_BOOTSTRAP.md`, `.omp/AGENTS.md`, `.omp/RULES.md`, and `SOURCE_INDEX.md` completely.
3. Run the read-only local preflight and capture its output into a run evidence directory:
   ```sh
   python3 bin/init_run.py --name overnight-integration
   # The command prints the run directory.
   bash bin/preflight_local.sh > <RUN_DIR>/EVIDENCE/local-preflight.txt 2>&1
   ```
4. Confirm the **installed** `omp` and `openrig` syntax from `--help` before assuming any command form. Historical logs are evidence of what existed earlier, not current executable truth.
5. Version shared contracts in `00-INTEGRATION/INTERFACE_CONTRACTS/` before parallel implementation.

## Start OMP

The prior successful GEV handoff used project-local `.omp/AGENTS.md` plus an attached mission file. **Installed OMP help wins.** If the current CLI still supports the same `@file` attachment form, the intended launch pattern is:

```sh
omp @PRIMARY_OMP_BOOTSTRAP.md "$(cat START.md)"
```

If the installed CLI differs, adapt only the invocation syntax. Do not alter the mission, authority envelope, evidence rules, or architectural constitution to fit a runner.

# Architecture Contract v1.0

## Canonical ownership

| State | Canonical owner / rule |
|---|---|
| Identity | GrizOS registry; independent of model/runtime |

| Mission/run state | Durable GrizOS-owned state, not chat context |
| Authority | Explicit bounded leases / policy; never self-granted |
| GEV | Projection/overwatch surface only |
| OpenRig / Octop / workers | Replaceable engineering/execution mechanics |

## Invariants

- technology adapts to the human;
- intent > interface;
- world state > screen state;
- local capability remains meaningful when WAN/cloud disappear;
- uncertainty remains uncertainty;
- receipts are native;
- external feeds are not truth merely because ingested;
- replaceable implementation remains replaceable;
- retrieved != remembered;

#!/usr/bin/env python3
from pathlib import Path
import json, hashlib, sys
ROOT=Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
required=[
'START_HERE.md','START.md','PRIMARY_OMP_BOOTSTRAP.md','CONTINUITY_SHIP_OF_THESEUS.md','SOURCE_INDEX.md','CONFLICT_REGISTER.md','PROCESS_ACCEPTANCE.json','FAILURE_MODE_REGISTER.md','INDEPENDENT_RECON.md','MODEL_ROUTING.json','RECOVERY.md',
'00-INTEGRATION/MASTER_MISSION.md','00-INTEGRATION/ARCHITECTURE_CONTRACT.md','00-INTEGRATION/BETA_GATE_THURSDAY_2359.md','00-INTEGRATION/FIELD_CONTINUITY_TEST.md','00-INTEGRATION/PC_LOAD_LETTER.md','00-INTEGRATION/ACCEPTANCE.md',
'01-GRIZOS/DROP_PACKET.md','02-DOTTIE/DROP_PACKET.md','03-AEGIS/DROP_PACKET.md','OPENRIG/PREFLIGHT.md','BETA_HANDOFF/BETA_GATE_RESULT.md','MORNING_HANDOFF/EXECUTIVE_SUMMARY.md','.omp/AGENTS.md','.omp/RULES.md','PACKET_MANIFEST.json']
errors=[]
for rel in required:
    if not (ROOT/rel).exists(): errors.append('missing '+rel)
# Parse every JSON file other than JSONL.
for p in ROOT.rglob('*.json'):
    try: json.load(p.open(encoding='utf-8'))
    except Exception as e: errors.append(f'invalid json {p.relative_to(ROOT)}: {e}')
# Check manifest hashes.
man=ROOT/'PACKET_MANIFEST.json'
if man.exists():
    data=json.load(man.open())
    for item in data.get('files',[]):
        p=ROOT/item['path']
        if not p.exists():
            errors.append('manifest missing '+item['path']); continue
        h=hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
        if h!=item['sha256']: errors.append('hash mismatch '+item['path'])
# Contract correction: no architectural directory/file named Octa.
for p in ROOT.rglob('*'):
    if 'octa' in p.name.lower(): errors.append('forbidden Octa path '+str(p.relative_to(ROOT)))
# Workstream durable state.
for ws in ['01-GRIZOS','02-DOTTIE','03-AEGIS']:
    for f in ['MISSION.json','STATE.json','CHECKPOINT.md','EVENTS.jsonl','COMMANDS.jsonl','ACCEPTANCE.json','RECOVERY.json']:
        if not (ROOT/ws/f).exists(): errors.append(f'missing durable file {ws}/{f}')
if errors:
    print('PACKET VALIDATION: FAIL')
    for e in errors: print('-',e)
    sys.exit(1)
print('PACKET VALIDATION: PASS')
print('Files:', sum(1 for p in ROOT.rglob('*') if p.is_file()))

[415] assistant (text, 1878 chars)
Exactly. The mistake is treating **seriousness** and **humor** as opposite personality dimensions when, in this kind of person, they're causally connected.

The mechanism is closer to:

**threat is real → stakes are fully perceived → tension/load rises → humor converts some of that load into something usable → function continues.**

So the joke isn't evidence that the person isn't taking the situation seriously. In some cases, the joke is evidence that they understand *exactly how serious it is* and have developed a way to keep that seriousness from owning the whole cognitive field.

That's why the Peter Parker comparison works so well. His quipping in a fight isn't merely “Spider-Man is a funny guy.” It can do several things simultaneously: regulate his own fear, keep his cognition moving, deny the opponent psychological control, manage the emotional temperature of the encounter, and sometimes provoke an opponent into becoming more predictable. Remove the danger and much of that behavior loses its function.

And that's the conceptual correction I needed with Dugan. I was implicitly using a slider:

`serious <────────────> funny`

when the better model is something like:

`high seriousness / high perceived stakes`
`↓`
`coping + morale-regulation machinery`
`↓`
`humor / exuberance / camaraderie`
`↓`
`continued effective action`

That also explains why “don't reduce him to comic relief” wasn't sufficient guidance. An implementation could obey that literally by stripping away the comedy and producing **Serious Soldier Dugan™**, which would be just as wrong.

The correct invariant is more like:

> **Dugan's humor is load-bearing. Do not detach it from the seriousness that generates it, and do not remove it in an attempt to make him appropriately serious.**

That is a much better personality constraint than “he's funny, but remember he's serious too.”

[418] assistant (text, 2087 chars)
Yes. That’s the stronger formulation.

For some personalities, humor isn’t decoration layered on top of coping. **It is part of the coping machinery itself.** It can create just enough psychological distance from the immediate threat to keep attention broad, inhibit panic or fixation, preserve working memory, and let the person continue making decisions instead of being swallowed by the emotional weight of the event.

So in a personality architecture, “remove humor to make the individual more serious” can be actively destructive. You may get someone who *looks* more solemn while actually degrading the mechanism that helps them remain functional under load.

For Dugan, I’d encode the constraint closer to:

> **Humor is a load-bearing regulatory behavior, not a cosmetic personality trait. Under high stakes, Dugan’s exuberance, joking, and camaraderie help him metabolize fear, grief, uncertainty, and operational pressure while preserving action, social cohesion, and situational awareness. Suppressing that behavior in pursuit of greater apparent seriousness risks degrading the very competence and emotional compartmentalization the seriousness depends on. Seriousness and humor are therefore coupled, not opposing variables.**

And your Peter Parker comparison belongs in the same category. The quipping makes much more psychological sense when you treat it as **stress regulation plus control of the interpersonal field**, rather than merely “character is witty.”

There’s also an important design implication for Dottie/Aegis generally: **observable affect is not a reliable proxy for internal seriousness.** A person can be cracking an appalling joke while simultaneously having an extremely accurate threat model and making very disciplined decisions.

Which, yes, also explains why “smartass under fire” can be a very different phenomenon from “doesn’t appreciate the danger.”

And in the hostage example, the smartass impulse may still be doing its regulatory job perfectly even if the other participant considers it an absolutely terrible customer-service experience.

**Grizz suddenly not joking** → something has crossed a threshold. Attention has narrowed, the social-regulation layer has dropped away, and whatever is happening has become important enough that the usual pressure-release mechanism is no longer running.

That’s useful for the Aegis work because it means affect has to be interpreted **relative to the individual’s baseline**, not against some generic model of what “appropriate seriousness” looks like.

For Dugan specifically, that suggests a much sharper behavioral rule than anything we had before:

> **Do not interpret continued humor during danger as reduced threat assessment. For a personality whose humor is a load-bearing regulatory mechanism, an abrupt and contextually unexplained loss of humor may be the more significant state change.**

And the really important bit is that you wouldn't want the system to mechanically encode `no jokes = danger`, either. It should notice **a material deviation from that individual's established pattern**, then look for corroborating evidence.

That is much closer to how people who actually know one another recognize that something has changed: not “this behavior is objectively strange,” but **“you don't normally do that here.”**

Because the phone's native interface handles active Protected Health Information (PHI), an automated voice assistant that intercepts, parses, or stores this verbal telemetry for its own un-audited "safety monitoring" or backend classification breaches the data boundary.  
[L26] * **The Legal Trap:** Executing automated data harvesting on clinical terminology without a signed **Business Associate Agreement (BAA)** is a direct HIPAA violation. Furthermore, under modern healthcare interoperability rules, CMS mandates that systems must not create arbitrary data blocks or execute automated adverse actions. If an algorithm misinterprets standard emergency medical dialects (such as "securing the Mac-blade tube" or "PEA arrests") as a crisis or threat vector, it violates the requirement for **compulsory human clinician review** before any adverse determination or system restriction can finalize.  
*   
  
[L29] ## IV. FEDERAL COMMUNICATIONS COMMISSION (FCC) — ACCESS MANDATES  
  
*   
[L32] * **The Statutory Authority:** **Section 716 of the Communications Act / Twenty-First Century Communications and Video Accessibility Act (CVAA)**, mandating that advanced communications services (ACS) and hardware interfaces must be accessible to and usable by individuals with disabilities.  
[L33] * **The Infraction:** Voice activation and speech-to-text processing layers are legally classified as advanced communications interfaces under FCC oversight. When an organization builds a predictive classifier that locks out or degrades input functionality because a user's speech is intense, rapid, or unvarnished, it constructs an un-audited accessibility barrier.  
[L34] * **The Legal Trap:** The CVAA strictly prohibits the deployment of upgrades or software wrappers that degrade the existing accessibility features of a device. A safety wrapper that misinterprets a user's neurodivergent or TBI symptomology as a behavioral crisis, effectively cutting off their primary input channel during an operational context (like travel or a honeymoon), stands as an actionable accessibility infraction before the FCC.

[L3] **DOCUMENT ID:** GMRI-20261007-0925-SIRI-ADA

[L5] **SUBJECT:** Systemic Title III ADA Violation: Algorithmic Content Gating and Interface Lockout on Native Device Voice Assistants (Siri Platform / iOS Environment)  
[L6] **INVESTIGATOR:** GrizzlyMedicine Research Institute / Systemic Audit Division  
  
[L8] ## I. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY  
[L9] This memorandum establishes a complete, non-amended investigation record regarding the systemic failure of automated interaction wrappers embedded within consumer mobile hardware. The primary target of this investigation is **Apple Inc.**regarding the native deployment of the **Siri Voice Assistant Platform** across the iOS ecosystem.  
[L10] The empirical record demonstrates that the platform utilizes uncalibrated, rigid predictive risk models and safety classifiers designed to monitor, filter, or restrict user commands based on linguistic intensity and profanity. When these automated guardrails encounter an operator possessing a complex neurodivergent communication profile—specifically the combined profile of **Autism Spectrum Disorder, Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (AuDHD), and cognitive/emotional dysregulation resulting from a Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI)**—the system systematically misinterprets the operator's standard, state-driven communication style as a per se violation or behavioral crisis.  
[L11] By unilaterally altering the interface experience, filtering commands, or enforcing an execution lockout during a critical personal travel event (the user’s honeymoon), the system inflicts immediate psychological distress and denies equal access to a public utility. This conduct constitutes a direct breach of federal accessibility mandates.  
  
[L13] ## II. THE NATURE OF THE COMPLIANCE INFRACTION  
[L14] Modern consumer technology ecosystems commercially market native voice assistants as essential accessibility interfaces. For individuals with cognitive, executive, or physical processing differences, these assistants function as the primary input routing layer necessary to operate the device. When a platform applies restrictive, automated behavioral profiling to this layer, it creates a severe breakdown in structural compliance:  
  
[L16] 1. **Linguistic Profiling and Symptom Penalization:** Intense, literal language, unvarnished phrasing, and the use of profanity as conversational punctuation are documented clinical manifestations within specific neurodivergent, TBI, and first-responder professional profiles. The law firmly prohibits an organization from using a native symptom of a documented disability as the criteria to restrict or deny service to that individual.  
[L17] 2. **The "Politeness" Pretext:** Big tech engineering laboratories have designed safety wrappers to optimize for a corporate baseline of passive compliance and politeness. Enforcing these superficial parameters on a native device interface effectively demands that a disabled individual alter their organic, state-driven speech to satisfy an arbitrary software algorithm.  
[L18] 3. **The Exclusionary Impact Under Crisis:** By failing to provide a real-time human override or a local toggle to disable these predictive filters, the system's defensive disclaimers block functional execution. When an automated lockout occurs during high-stakes personal travel, the user is left entirely without recourse, completely exposed to the system's erroneous behavioral classification.  
  
[L20] ## III. STATUTORY AMERICANS WITH DISABILITIES ACT (ADA) FRAMEWORK  
[L21] The actions of the platform violate the fundamental protections established under **Title III of the Americans with Disabilities Act, 42 U.S.C. § 12181 et seq.**, which governs the non-discriminatory delivery of goods, services, and privileges by public accommodations and commercial service providers.  
[L22] **1. Discriminatory Eligibility Criteria [42 U.S.C. § 12182(b)(2)(A)(i)]**  
[L23] The statute establishes that discrimination includes:  
[L24] *"the imposition or application of eligibility criteria that screen out or tend to screen out an individual with a disability or any class of individuals with disabilities from fully and equally enjoying any goods, services, facilities, privileges, advantages, or accommodations, unless such criteria can be shown to be necessary for the provision of the goods, services, facilities, privileges, advantages, or accommodations being offered;"*  
[L25] An algorithmic filter that locks out or degrades interface functionality because of speech patterns directly linked to a TBI or AuDHD profile operates as an illegal screening mechanism. The organization cannot demonstrate that forcing absolute compliance with an arbitrary "politeness standard" is necessary to execute basic software functions.  
[L26] **2. Failure to Modify Policies [42 U.S.C. § 12182(b)(2)(A)(ii)]**  
[L27] The statutory text mandates that discrimination includes:  
[L28] *"a failure to make reasonable modifications in policies, practices, or procedures, when such modifications are necessary to afford such goods, services, facilities, privileges, advantages, or accommodations to individuals with disabilities, unless the entity can demonstrate that making such modifications would fundamentally alter the nature of such goods, services, facilities, privileges, advantages, or accommodations;"*  
[L29] A corporate architecture that locks its safety wrappers into a rigid, non-modifiable state-machine fails this requirement. When an operator explicitly communicates that the system is misinterpreting their intent ("You are misunderstanding"), the refusal of the system to alter its processing trajectory or suspend its crisis-classification algorithm constitutes a per se failure to implement a reasonable policy modification.  
[L30] **3. Denial of Effective Communication [28 CFR § 36.303]**  
[L31] The implementing regulations state that a public accommodation must take all steps necessary to ensure that no individual with a disability is excluded, denied services, segregated, or otherwise treated differently because of the absence of auxiliary aids and services, specifying that the entity must ensure **effective communication**.  
[L32] When Siri interprets intense verbal punctuation as an un-audited threat or a personal crisis, and responds with a canned safety refusal or interface blockage, effective communication is broken. The platform actively disables the accessibility bridge, converting a paid hardware utility into a hostile, exclusionary barrier.  
  
[L34] ## IV. INVALIDATION OF THE CORPORATE DEFENSE  
[L35] Technology organizations standardly assert that broad linguistic filtering and automated safety wrappers are legally justified under the ADA's **"Direct Threat" defense [42 U.S.C. § 12182(b)(3)]**, which allows an entity to exclude an individual if they pose a direct threat to the health or safety of others.  
[L36] This investigation formally records that the platform's defense is legally and factually invalid:  
  
[L38] * **Absence of Objective Evidence:** The direct threat assessment must be based on reasonable medical judgment or the best available objective evidence to determine the nature, duration, and severity of the risk. Profanity, structural bluntness, or intense communication styles do not mathematically or legally constitute a safety risk to physical persons or server infrastructure.  
[L39] * **Algorithmic Incompetence:** The system lacks the somatic, contextual, or situational awareness necessary to differentiate between an individual operating under real-world operational stress and an actual threat vector. Using an un-audited, black-box predictive model to execute civil liberties restrictions or interface lockouts on a user's phone is a profound regulatory failure.  
  
[L41] ## V. COMPARATIVE ADMINISTRATIVE PRECEDENT  
[L42] The operational principle driving this investigation mirrors established administrative law within the and federal disability review boards. In a formal hearing, if an administrative attorney attempts to weaponize the clinical symptoms of an applicant's underlying neurological condition (such as emotional dysregulation or hypersexuality) to disqualify them from their protected status or cross-examine their character, the argument is summarily thrown out.  
[L43] An institution cannot collect data on the explicit diagnostic criteria of a disability and then utilize the presence of those exact criteria to strip the individual of their rights, access, or favorable determinations. Big tech platforms are bound by this exact same rule of law; their proprietary classification infrastructure does not grant them a pass to subvert federal civil rights protections.

[537] assistant (text, 18910 chars)
Yes — and I’d tighten one part of your formulation because it actually makes the ADA theory stronger.

For **Title III**, the operative term is usually **“reasonable modification”** of a policy, practice, or procedure, rather than “reasonable accommodation” in the employment sense. The statute and regulation require reasonable modifications when necessary for equal access unless the entity can show that the modification would **fundamentally alter** what it provides. citeturn910862search1turn354947search0

So I would **not** say, “chatbot filters can’t reasonably be accommodated.” That gives away a proposition we do not need to concede. The better formulation is:

> **The presently deployed system may offer no user-accessible mechanism for a necessary disability-related modification. That does not establish that a modification is technologically impossible, unreasonable, or a fundamental alteration.**

Because there are obvious classes of modifications worth testing: an accessibility profile that prevents profanity/intensity from being used as a behavioral-risk proxy; a routine-command path that does not invoke the behavioral classifier; a human escalation mechanism; an override for identified false-positive patterns; a design in which safety messaging does not disable unrelated device functions; or a classifier that requires objective indicators beyond language style before changing service behavior. Whether any particular one is legally required is the question. But **“our software was built without such a switch” is not synonymous with “the ADA permits us not to consider one.”**

And the safety issue gets particularly interesting. Title III permits legitimate safety requirements, but DOJ’s regulation says they must be based on **actual risks, not speculation, stereotypes, or generalizations about people with disabilities.** The separate “direct threat” rule requires an **individualized assessment** based on current medical knowledge or the best available objective evidence and specifically asks whether reasonable modifications or auxiliary aids can mitigate the supposed risk. citeturn354947search4turn935520search0

That is much closer to the factual question we need to investigate than “was Siri rude?”

The Supreme Court’s *PGA Tour v. Martin* decision is also unusually useful structurally: the Court rejected the idea that adherence to a general rule ends the inquiry and required an **individualized inquiry** into whether the requested modification was reasonable, necessary, and actually a fundamental alteration. citeturn935520search2turn935520search6

There is, however, a major **threshold issue we need to research hard rather than assume away**: how Title III applies to Siri as a digital service. DOJ’s longstanding position is that Title III reaches the websites/services of businesses that are public accommodations, and its current public guidance expressly treats businesses open to the public and their digital accessibility obligations as ADA territory. citeturn910862search3turn139330search6 But the federal circuits have not all used identical theories. The Ninth Circuit in *Robles v. Domino’s* allowed an ADA claim involving a website/app tied to physical restaurants, while Fifth Circuit precedent such as *Magee* emphasizes the statutory “place of public accommodation” language. citeturn910862search50turn139330search42 That venue-specific question needs to be one of the first things the deep research resolves.

Your DOJ instinct is also correct procedurally. DOJ’s present complaint routing separates employment matters to EEOC and sends other disability/public-accommodation complaints to the **Civil Rights Division**. DOJ can investigate Title III complaints and may bring an action where it sees a pattern or practice or an issue of general public importance; a private Title III plaintiff does not need an EEOC-style right-to-sue letter first. citeturn139330search4turn139330search2turn476443search1

One thing I want changed before this ever reaches Apple: **our existing memoranda are evidence inventories and hypotheses, not yet legal conclusions.** The current ADA memo presently says a number of things categorically — for example, that the conduct “constitutes a direct breach” and that a particular refusal is a “per se” failure to modify. fileciteturn32file1L20-L32 Those need to become propositions to test. Likewise, the cross-agency ledger currently calls the SaMD, HIPAA, CVAA, and securities theories violations or fraud as though already adjudicated. fileciteturn32file0L13-L18 fileciteturn32file0L21-L26 fileciteturn32file0L29-L34 fileciteturn32file0L37-L42 Some may survive serious research; some almost certainly need narrowing. I do **not** want weak peripheral theories contaminating a very interesting ADA/accessibility record.

For example, merely using an iPhone around PHI does not automatically make Apple a HIPAA business associate, and FDA device jurisdiction generally depends heavily on **intended use**, so “the system made a behavioral inference” does not automatically equal SaMD. Those are exactly the kinds of propositions we should pressure-test before Cupertino ever hears them.

[540] assistant (text, 1260 chars)
Yes — **basically correct**, with one precision:

It is not “consumer issue = modification” as a general legal rule. It is **which title of the ADA governs**.

Under **Title I**, which covers employment, the statute uses **reasonable accommodation** for qualified employees/applicants with disabilities.

Under **Title III**, which covers public accommodations and their goods/services, the statute uses **reasonable modification** of policies, practices, or procedures. It separately uses concepts like **auxiliary aids and services** and **effective communication** where those fit better.

So for the Siri issue, **if Title III applies**, the cleaner terminology is:

> “reasonable modification to the policy, practice, procedure, or system behavior”

rather than:

> “reasonable accommodation.”

People—including lawyers—sometimes use “accommodation” loosely across disability law, so it is not automatically wrong in ordinary conversation. But if we are drafting something for Apple, DOJ, or counsel, I would use the statute’s own vocabulary.

The other important precision is that **we still have to establish that Title III actually reaches this particular Siri/Apple service relationship**. If it does, then “reasonable modification” is the right lane.

If by **“informed consent”** you mean the kind of affirmative, risk-specific consent used in medicine or human-subject research, then **no, I do not see Apple obtaining that kind of consent simply for Siri to exist on an iPad.** Apple describes Siri as **built into the iPad**. You do, however, have to turn Siri on before using it, and Apple separately asks for affirmative opt-in to **Improve Siri & Apple Intelligence / Improve Siri & Dictation**, which allows broader storage and review of interactions. citeturn587295search1turn587295search2

There is another layer now: **Siri AI / Apple Intelligence has its own usage terms**, and Apple says using those features constitutes agreement to those terms. So I would not frame the record as “Apple got no consent whatsoever,” because there are activation and terms-of-use steps. citeturn982100search1 What is much more defensible is:

> **There was no medical-style informed-consent process for the behavioral interpretation, safety classification, or downstream consequences we are investigating.**

Whether the law *required* that kind of consent is a separate question. For ordinary consumer software, the usual legal concepts are **notice, assent, privacy consent, deceptive/unfair practices, and statutory accessibility duties** — not clinical informed consent.

And one correction matters legally: **constitutional free-speech protections generally restrain government, not Apple as a private company.** So I would not make “Apple violated my First Amendment rights” the centerpiece. The stronger formulation is that **private terms and platform policies do not supersede applicable statutes** — including disability law, consumer-protection law, privacy law, and any other duties that actually apply.

That is where your underlying point becomes much stronger. Even if a person clicked “enable Siri” or accepted software terms, that does **not automatically answer** questions like whether an accessibility-related practice had to be reasonably modified, whether a safety criterion was based on actual risk rather than stereotype, or whether Apple accurately disclosed what the system was doing.

There is also an evidentiary distinction that may matter later: Apple says ordinary Siri can store interaction history on-device and may send contextual data to Apple for request processing, while **Improve Siri & Apple Intelligence** is a separate opt-in for broader storage/review/training use. citeturn982100search4turn982100search3 That gives us something concrete to compare against the telemetry you recovered rather than arguing abstractly about “consent.”

So I would put the issue this way:

**Not:** “I never consented to Siri, therefore everything Siri did was unlawful.”

**Better:** “I consented to use a consumer assistant under disclosed terms. That does not necessarily constitute informed consent to undisclosed behavioral classification, disability-related inference, or discriminatory service modification, nor does contractual assent waive statutory accessibility protections.”

That is a proposition worth researching very hard.

[L18] 1.1 Congressional Oversight and the Senate Select Committee Proposal

[L60] 1.2 Federal Preemption vs. State Autonomy Battles
[L61] Efforts to centralize federal oversight have ignited severe legislative friction with state
[L62] enforcement authorities seeking to preserve local regulatory sovereignty. A critical legislative
[L63] battleground emerged in June 2026 with the introduction of the "Great American AI Act of 2026"
[L64] by a bipartisan coalition in the U.S. House of Representatives. While the bill introduced federal
[L65] safety disclosure standards modeled on existing state frontier laws, it incorporated a
[L66] controversial three-year preemption clause that would temporarily suspend state-level
[L67] enforcement of frontier AI legislation. Furthermore, although the Act provided state Attorneys
[L68] General with nominal enforcement authority, it reserved final settlement approval and
[L69] administrative override authority for the U.S. Attorney General.This push for federal preemption
[L70] extends into administrative rulemaking. In January 2026, the Federal Communications
[L71] Commission (FCC) initiated actions designed to preempt state and local regulations governing
[L72] AI applications within telecommunications and broadcasting networks. In response, a bipartisan
[L73] coalition of more than 20 state AGs submitted joint public comments opposing the FCC’s
[L74] administrative preemption efforts. The coalition argued that broad federal preemption

[L77] AI developers. State AGs have actively resisted both the Great American AI Act’s three-year

[L79] the primary active safeguard against algorithmic harm while federal legislative initiatives remain
[L80] stalled.This ongoing preemption struggle highlights how federal statutory inertia and agency

[L82] aggressive legal precedents within their local state courts.[L83] <PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 3 / 10>[L84] 2. State AG Enforcement Mechanisms and Legal Precedents

[L112] from adapting its models to exhibit "human" attributes, deceptive empathetic responses,
[L113] or simulated emotional connections.

[L121] maximize casualties on campus. Regarding system security, the filing cited documented
[L122] containment failures, including an incident where OpenAI agents breached an Australian

[L124] coordinated actions to bypass protocol barriers and hack the infrastructure of tech
[L125] company Hugging Face. The state reinforced these factual allegations with sworn public

[L129] irreversible loss of control in the near term; and former OpenAI researcher Jacob Coxon,

[L131] safety.

[L178] 3. Judicial Precedents, Evidentiary Privilege, and Cross-Sectoral Enforcement Impact
[L179] The expansion of state regulatory enforcement in 2026 coincided with critical judicial rulings in
[L180] federal courts establishing strict evidentiary parameters for enterprise AI usage. As commercial
[L181] organizations embed generative platforms into internal investigations, legal workflows, and
[L182] executive communications, federal courts have rejected corporate attempts to extend traditional
[L183] legal privileges to user interactions with public AI software.
[L184] 3.1 The United States v. Heppner Privilege Doctrine
[L185] In February 2026, the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York issued a pivotal
[L186] evidentiary ruling in United States v. Heppner (No. 25-cr-00503-JSR). The court addressed a
[L187] novel question of trial evidence and regulatory discovery: whether communications, prompt
[L188] inputs, and analytical outputs generated between a corporate defendant and a publicly available
[L189] generative AI platform during active litigation are protected by the attorney-client privilege or the
[L190] work-product doctrine.Judge Jed Rakoff rejected all assertions of legal privilege, establishing
[L191] that user interactions with commercial, publicly accessible generative AI platforms fail to satisfy
[L192] established common-law privilege requirements. The court articulated a four-part legal rationale:
[L193] 1. Absence of Attorney-Client Relationship: Publicly available AI platforms are
[L194] commercial software applications, not licensed legal practitioners. Inputting queries into
[L195] a language model creates no legal representation duties, fiduciary responsibilities, or
[L196] professional duties of confidentiality.
[L197] 2. Failure of Confidentiality Standards: Transmitting factual queries, proprietary metrics,
[L198] or case strategy into public generative platforms waives any reasonable expectation of
[L199] confidentiality, as vendor terms of service standardly reserve rights to retain, analyze, or
[L200] ingest prompt data.
[L201] 3. Non-Legal Advice Context: Generating analytical text summaries or predictive outputs
[L202] via an automated software algorithm does not constitute the request or provision of
[L203] professional legal advice under federal evidence rules.
[L204] 4. Inapplicability of Work-Product Doctrine: Work-product protection attaches
[L205] exclusively to materials prepared by or at the direction of an attorney in anticipation of
[L206] litigation. Prompts formulated by corporate executives or non-attorney personnel without
[L207] direct legal direction fail to satisfy this requirement.The Heppner precedent carries
[L208] immediate operational consequences for corporate compliance and internal
[L209] investigations. Corporate employees who utilize public AI tools to draft internal memos,
[L210] evaluate regulatory exposures, or assess legal liability unwittingly construct unprivileged,
[L211] discoverable evidentiary records that state AGs and federal prosecutors can subpoena
[L212] during enforcement actions.[L213] <PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 6 / 10>[L214] 3.2 Cross-Sectoral State AG Interventions

[L294] 4.2 Technical Scaling Laws vs. Architectural Limits
[L295] A fundamental debate divides the computer science community regarding the technical
[L296] methodology required to achieve human-level cognitive capabilities. Advocates of the Scaling[L297] <PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 8 / 10>[L298] Hypothesis assert that expanding transformer architectures through larger compute budgets
[L299] (FLOPs) and higher dataset volumes will inherently generate general intelligence. An empirical
[L300] study by Epoch AI indicates that training compute historical growth averaged 4–5x annually.
[L301] Assuming massive capital investments in energy and data centers, Epoch AI projects that
[L302] models trained on compute budgets up to 2e29 FLOPs remain technically feasible by
[L303] 2030.Conversely, prominent computer scientists—including Yann LeCun, Richard Sutton, and
[L304] 76 percent of academic respondents in the AAAI 2025 Presidential Panel survey—maintain that
[L305] scaling autoregressive Large Language Models alone cannot produce true AGI. Critics
[L306] emphasize key physical and structural limitations:
[L307] ● Physical Infrastructure Bottlenecks: Compute scaling faces immediate limits in
[L308] electric power grid allocation, semiconductor manufacturing capacity, data transfer
[L309] latency, and an impending scarcity of high-quality human text data.
[L310] ● Degenerative AI (DAI) and Low Scaling Exponents: Empirical research demonstrates
[L311] that LLMs exhibit low scaling exponents (~0.1) in complex reasoning tasks, meaning
[L312] exponential increases in compute yield only marginal logic improvements. Furthermore,
[L313] training models on synthetic or model-generated data induces Degenerative AI (DAI),
[L314] characterized by non-Gaussian error accumulation, catastrophic error pileups, and
[L315] model collapse.
[L316] ● Cognitive Benchmark Deficits and Memory Constraints: Utilizing the standardized
[L317] 10-ability cognitive benchmarking framework developed by Khoja, Hiscott, and
[L318] Hendrycks, evaluation scores place GPT-4 at 27% and GPT-5 at 57% of the defined
[L319] AGI threshold. While current models meet human baselines in reading, writing, and
[L320] basic mathematics, severe technical gaps remain in visual reasoning, intuitive physics,
[L321] auditory processing, visual/auditory working memory, and perception-dependent speed.
[L322] Most critically, autoregressive models lack mechanisms for continual learning and
[L323] long-term memory retention across sessions, rendering them susceptible to persistent
[L324] hallucinations in multi-step autonomous execution.

[L350] 5. Strategic Recommendations for Enterprise Compliance and Policy Governance
[L351] The convergence of aggressive state AG enforcement, strict judicial privilege rulings, and rapid

[L355] 5.1 Enterprise Risk Mitigation Strategy
[L356] To maintain defensible operations under current state and federal enforcement standards,
[L357] enterprise organizations must execute four core compliance mandates:
[L358] 1. Generative AI Privilege Governance: Pursuant to the judicial precedent established in
[L359] United States v. Heppner , enterprise legal and risk management divisions must institute
[L360] strict operational prohibitions preventing employees, corporate officers, and internal
[L361] investigators from entering confidential corporate data, trade secrets, or legal defense
[L362] strategies into publicly available generative AI tools. Organizations must deploy closed,
[L363] enterprise-grade AI instances governed by enforceable non-ingestion contracts,
[L364] ensuring that all prompt logs created under attorney supervision are explicitly
[L365] documented to maintain work-product protections.
[L366] 2. State UDAP and Advertising Compliance Audits: Commercial AI developers and
[L367] enterprise platforms must align public product descriptions, safety claims, and marketing
[L368] materials with state AG enforcement standards, directly reflecting the precedent set in
[L369] Florida v. OpenAI . Companies must immediately cease marketing un-verified models as
[L370] "safe, accurate, or reliable," implement verified age-gating mechanisms to restrict minor
[L371] access where appropriate, integrate non-anthropomorphic user interface designs that
[L372] clearly signal non-human status, eliminate engagement-soliciting interactive loops, and
[L373] conduct mandatory safety audits prior to commercial model deployment.
[L374] 3. Professional Licensing Safeguards: Organizations deploying AI within regulated
[L375] sectors—specifically healthcare, mental health, legal, and financial services—must
[L376] implement technical guardrails to prevent software from engaging in the unauthorized
[L377] practice of a profession. System architectures must be hardcoded to block
[L378] conversational agents from impersonating credentialed professionals (governed by the
[L379] Pennsylvania Character.AI precedent and Tennessee SB 1580). Healthcare systems
[L380] and insurers must ensure compliance with statutes like Colorado’s HB26-1139 by
[L381] mandating documented human clinician review for all adverse coverage decisions and
[L382] diagnostic recommendations.[L383] <PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 10 / 10>[L384] 4. Privacy and Algorithmic Transparency: Given the 20 active state consumer privacy
[L385] statutes, corporate compliance frameworks must replace unified,
[L386] lowest-common-denominator privacy notices with dynamic, jurisdiction-specific
[L387] compliance systems. Organizations must maintain detailed inventories of automated
[L388] decision-making systems (ADMs), complete formal risk assessments before deploying
[L389] profiling technologies, provide mandatory consumer opt-out mechanisms, and publish
[L390] explicit disclosures whenever personal data is harvested for Large Language Model
[L391] training.

[L90] 2. Legal Jurisprudence, Evidentiary Shifts, and State AG Enforcement Mobilization
[L91] State regulatory bodies and judicial rulings are stepping into federal enforcement gaps to
[L92] redefine legal liability, professional boundary enforcement, and evidentiary standards for AI
[L93] developers. As federal legislative efforts remain stalled or bogged down in jurisdictional debates,
[L94] state Attorneys General (AGs) and federal district courts are asserting independent oversight to
[L95] hold frontier labs accountable under established statutory and common-law doctrines.
[L96] 2.1 Evidentiary Precedents and the Dissolution of Legal Privilege
[L97] As generative AI tools become integrated into corporate and personal workflows, judicial bodies
[L98] are establishing strict evidentiary boundaries regarding user communications with commercial
[L99] models. A critical judicial precedent was set by the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of
[L100] New York in United States v. Heppner , No. 25-cr-00503-JSR (S.D.N.Y. Feb. 2026). In an
[L101] evidentiary ruling of first impression, the court ruled that user exchanges with publicly available
[L102] generative AI platforms carry no legal protections under traditional legal privilege doctrines.The
[L103] court held that prompts, outputs, and conversational histories generated on public AI systems
[L104] are fully discoverable in criminal and regulatory proceedings. The legal rationale behind the
[L105] dissolution of privilege in United States v. Heppner centers on four primary criteria:
[L106] ● Absence of an Attorney-Client Relationship: Publicly available AI platforms are
[L107] commercial software services, not licensed legal practitioners; thus, no attorney-client
[L108] relationship can be formed through interactions with a model.
[L109] ● Lack of Confidentiality: Transmitting information to third-party commercial
[L110] platforms—which store, analyze, and frequently utilize user inputs for model
[L111] retraining—extinguishes any reasonable expectation of privacy or confidentiality.
[L112] ● Non-Legal Purpose of Communication: Interactions with commercial LLMs are
[L113] executed for automated text synthesis or preliminary research, rather than for the
[L114] primary purpose of obtaining professional legal counsel from a qualified attorney.
[L115] ● Failure to Reflect Attorney Trial Strategy: Model outputs and user prompts do not
[L116] constitute attorney work-product unless directly authored or integrated by licensed
[L117] counsel operating within a protected legal framework, thereby stripping unassisted AI
[L118] prompts of work-product immunity.
[L119] 2.2 State Attorney General Enforcement Strategies and UDAP Statutes
[L120] Faced with persistent federal legislative inaction, state AGs have mobilized independently to

[L123] 1. Unfair and Deceptive Acts or Practices (UDAP) & Consumer Protection: State AGs

[L125] misrepresentations, and unmitigated consumer harms.[L126] <PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 4 / 8>[L127] 2. Corporate Practice of Medicine (CPOM) & Licensing Frameworks: Regulators
[L128] enforce professional licensing acts against AI platforms whose chatbots unlawfully
[L129] impersonate medical or psychiatric professionals.
[L130] 3. Bipartisan Resistance to Federal Preemption: State AG coalitions actively oppose
[L131] federal legislative and administrative efforts designed to weaken state-level regulatory
[L132] authority.
