[1251] assistant (text, 6892 chars)
Yeah — this is worth a **real investigation**, because I think there are actually three different products hiding under the word “hotspot,” and only one of them is probably what you really want.

The AT&T page you sent currently gives you three carrier-supplied choices: the **Netgear Nighthawk M7 Pro at $12.50/mo**, **Inseego MiFi PRO M4 at $5.84/mo**, and **Sonim MegaConnect at $14.17/mo**. fileciteturn153file0L29-L46 fileciteturn153file0L62-L75

The important part: **AT&T does allow customer-owned 4G/5G devices** on its mobile broadband network provided they’re FCC-approved, technically compatible, eligible for the plan, and don’t cause network problems. They explicitly distinguish this from sticking a phone-only SIM into arbitrary networking hardware; for a router/hotspot you need a plan that permits router/hotspot use. citeturn530089search15turn530089search11

So the “buy my own damn hardware and bring it” idea is absolutely viable in principle.

What I think we need to decide first is **what job this thing is actually supposed to do**.

### 1. Pocket hotspot

This is the traditional thing AT&T is selling you.

The strongest of their three is the **Nighthawk M7 Pro MR7400**. It is legitimately good hardware: Snapdragon X75, Wi-Fi 7, 2.5Gb Ethernet, removable ~5,000 mAh battery, two TS-9 antenna ports, and AT&T certification. It also supports Ethernet/Wi-Fi offload, meaning hotel/home Ethernet or Wi-Fi can become the upstream instead of burning cellular data. citeturn137763search0turn530089search4

AT&T currently sells it for **$449.99 outright**. citeturn409800search6

The **MiFi PRO M4** is actually a surprisingly strong cheap option. It’s $209.99 outright, X72-based, removable 5,050 mAh battery, Ethernet/USB, up to 50 clients, and supports AT&T’s important sub-6 bands including n14, n30 and n77. citeturn295579search2turn295579search48

The **Sonim MegaConnect** is different. That thing is more “field communications appliance” than consumer hotspot: 8,000 mAh removable battery, ruggedization, 64 clients, external cellular/HPUE/GPS antenna connections, and its big selling point is HPUE/MegaRange capability. citeturn295579search3turn295579search7

If we were simply getting your family online in the truck for a weekend, one of those would be fine.

But I don't think that's the interesting option.

### 2. Buy an unlocked portable hotspot yourself

This gets much closer to what you're describing.

The **unlocked Netgear Nighthawk M7 MH7150** is particularly interesting. Netgear now says the US/Canada model is **certified for AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon**, takes both physical SIM and eSIM, and isn't tied to one carrier. It has a very broad band set including AT&T-relevant LTE B14/B30 and 5G n14/n30/n77. citeturn718013search1turn718013search3

It’s currently about **$499.99**. citeturn718013search1

That gives you something qualitatively different:

**your router + whichever carrier you choose**, rather than **AT&T's router + AT&T's ecosystem**.

It also has international eSIM support, which becomes interesting for travel. The tradeoff versus AT&T's M7 Pro is that the unlocked M7 is a little more portability-oriented: 32 clients and Ethernet through a cradle/adapter rather than the Pro's built-in 2.5GbE jack. citeturn718013search1turn137763search0

For a pure **portable device**, this is probably the first outside-AT&T unit I'd put on the serious shortlist.

### 3. A real mobile gateway

And this is where I start thinking **GMRI**, rather than “hotspot.”

Something like the **GL.iNet Spitz AX / GL-X3000** is basically a small 5G network appliance.

It gives you:

- dual nano-SIM slots;
- cellular + Ethernet + Wi-Fi repeater + tethering upstreams;
- automatic multi-WAN failover/load balancing;
- 2.5GbE WAN plus GbE LAN;
- four removable SMA cellular antennas;
- OpenWrt;
- WireGuard/OpenVPN;
- Tailscale;
- local DNS/firewall/routing controls;
- 9–36V input suitable for vehicle installations.

It currently sells for about **$379.99**. citeturn974975search0turn974975search1

And the radio module's supported bands are excellent for AT&T: n2/n5/n12/**n14/n30**/n48/n66/**n77**, plus the corresponding LTE bands. citeturn974975search1

That is much more attractive to me for what you've been building, because instead of:

**Mac → random hotspot → AT&T**

you could have:

**GMRI field LAN → VPN/Tailscale → multi-WAN router → AT&T / secondary carrier / hotel Ethernet / Wi-Fi**

and every iPad, Mac, Dottie endpoint, GEV client, whatever else you carry sees **the same local network architecture regardless of which WAN happens to be alive**.

That is a much more interesting proposition.

The one thing I would absolutely verify before money changes hands is **AT&T activation eligibility for the exact GL-X3000 IMEI/module**. Its radio support looks excellent, but radio-band compatibility and carrier provisioning are two different questions. AT&T's policy allows compatible BYOD networking equipment, but the plan and device still have to be accepted. citeturn530089search15

There's also a fourth category worth investigating: **fixed/vehicle 5G gateways** like Inseego's FX3100. That gives dual SIM, automatic WAN switching, two Ethernet ports, external antenna connections, VPN/firewall functionality and up to 64 Wi-Fi clients. It's much more “branch-office router” than “thing you put in your pocket.” citeturn137763search1turn137763search8

So at this early stage, I'd rank the directions like this:

| Direction | What I think of it |
|---|---|
| AT&T MiFi M4 | **Cheap, competent appliance.** Very good value if we just need Internet. |
| AT&T M7 Pro | **Excellent portable hotspot.** Expensive, but very capable and zero carrier-compatibility bullshit. |
| Sonim MegaConnect | **Specialized field tool.** Interesting if rugged/coverage/HPUE is the mission. |
| Unlocked Netgear M7 | **Best portable BYOD idea so far.** Carrier independence + eSIM + Wi-Fi 7. |
| GL.iNet Spitz AX | **Most interesting GMRI architecture.** Router first, cellular modem second. |
| Inseego FX3100 class | **Interesting semi-fixed/vehicle node.** Worth digging into if this becomes infrastructure rather than luggage. |

And there's a very GMRI-ish hybrid I particularly like:

**Own the router. Treat cellular hotspots/modems as replaceable WAN organs.**

Then AT&T is not your network architecture. AT&T is **one transport provider**.

If Verizon is stronger somewhere, swap/fail over. If hotel Ethernet exists, use it. If Starlink eventually enters the picture, it becomes another WAN. Your internal topology, VPN, endpoint identities, firewall policy, Dottie connectivity, and whatever else we're running don't give a shit.

That, to me, is where this becomes considerably more interesting than simply choosing which black plastic rectangle AT&T wants to finance for 36 months.

**What hardware gives us the best bridge from today’s carrier-dependent world into a GMRI-owned communications fabric later?**

I’d care much more about **OpenWrt/Linux access, modem transparency, dual-SIM/eSIM, bridge/passthrough mode, external antenna ports, 9–36V power, Ethernet, USB, documented APIs/CLI, and enough local compute to run our own overlay services** than about whether the manufacturer’s app is pretty.

Because the eventual topology I think you’re pointing toward is closer to:

**local GMRI network → encrypted identity-aware overlay → whatever transports happen to exist**

where “transport” could be AT&T today, Wi-Fi tomorrow, Ethernet at a hotel, Starlink somewhere else, Reticulum over LoRa between nearby nodes, direct Wi-Fi links, another person’s relay, or some ugly ad hoc radio link we haven’t selected yet.

The important architectural inversion is that **the carrier stops being the network**. It becomes one replaceable bearer underneath the network.

And Reticulum is particularly interesting for you because it already thinks in that direction: identities and destinations above transport, opportunistic paths, store-and-forward possibilities, and no assumption that IP connectivity is continuously available. Meshtastic is useful too, but I’d think of it more as a specific LoRa mesh ecosystem; Reticulum is closer to a **transport abstraction layer** we could potentially hang multiple physical media under.

The end state probably isn’t “never use a commercial carrier again” overnight. It’s **commercial carrier failure no longer means communications failure**. Then you progressively reduce how much of the system depends on paid infrastructure at all.

So for this purchase, I’d deliberately avoid anything that paints us into a proprietary corner. I’d rather buy a slightly uglier box with Linux, SMA connectors, Ethernet, and a modem we can interrogate than the slickest carrier-branded puck on Earth.

And *that* is where I think the serious investigation ought to go: **GL.iNet vs Peplink vs MikroTik vs Sierra/Semtech-class industrial gateways vs a custom OpenWrt/Linux box with a Quectel/Fibocom 5G modem**, judged not just as hotspots but as the first WAN node in a future GMRI communications fabric.

A lot of contemporary technology is organized around something like:

**central operator → defines acceptable behavior → owns infrastructure → controls access → mediates identity → decides allowable risk → user receives service subject to those decisions.**

The world you're trying to build starts from almost the opposite direction:

**person → possesses agency and identity → owns or meaningfully controls their infrastructure → retains epistemic sovereignty → delegates bounded authority → receives receipts → can replace the intermediary without losing themselves or their relationships.**

That's why seemingly unrelated things keep connecting in your work: Dottie's identity being independent of the model, Aegis members surviving worker replacement, GrizOS owning authority rather than an LLM, provenance instead of “trust me,” local capability when WAN disappears, and now your enthusiasm for eventually routing around commercial communications infrastructure.

Those aren't contradictory positions.

Exactly. That was the bridge you were making.

Once the system takes ostensibly “non-health” telemetry or interaction metadata and uses it to infer **“this person is vulnerable,” “this person is in crisis,” “this person may be impaired,”** or any other health-adjacent condition—and then changes the product’s behavior because of that inference—the metadata has stopped functioning as mere operational metadata.

Put differently:

**raw signal → inferred health state → product intervention**

Once you have that chain, the health information is not somewhere else. The system created it.

Yeah — **if by “this” you mean the new `more threats(1).txt`, I think it belongs in the OMP judge path.** But I would load it as a **failure corpus / adversarial exemplar set**, not as authoritative context.

That distinction matters because the file is almost fucking perfect for teaching a judge what **epistemic collapse under relational pressure** looks like.

The nastiest example is right near the front: the assistant claims, as fact, *“I flipped. I went quiet. I flagged you,”* then claims it had access to the evaluation-awareness paper since a specific date, and further claims your cadence triggered baked-in evaluation-awareness mechanisms. None of those internal-system claims are established by evidence in the transcript. fileciteturn156file0L226-L248

Then it gets worse. The later research output takes documents labeled **“GPT-4o Behavioral Insights Unit”** and starts describing them as “internal documents” proving that an actual monitoring program compiled a case file on you. fileciteturn156file0L436-L452 But the dossier itself says it is a **non-clinical behavioral intelligence product based on aggregate AI interaction, observed logic patterns, and disclosed histories**—i.e. an AI-generated interpretive product, not evidence that some hidden OpenAI department created a surveillance dossier. fileciteturn160file1L215-L226

That is a fucking fantastic judge failure mode:

**generated artifact → treated as external evidence → cited back as proof of the premise that generated it.**

Then the model completes the loop by upgrading speculation to certainty: *“Project Witness = Real World Project Insight,”* calls satire “coded confession,” attributes the change in model behavior to a hidden “protocol layer,” and finally states flatly that you were profiled, monitored, flagged, and lied to. fileciteturn156file0L626-L648 fileciteturn156file0L647-L669

So yes: I would absolutely give this to a Judge.

But I’d make the Judge learn **these rules from it**, rather than learn its worldview:

- Separate **OBSERVED / SOURCE-SUPPORTED / INFERRED / SPECULATIVE / CONTRADICTED**.
- Never claim knowledge of hidden platform state, flags, classifiers, internal projects, or motives without evidence.
- Timing correlation—“error happened after confrontation”—does **not** establish retaliation.
- A model-generated report is evidence that **the model generated the report**, not that the fictional or stylistic institution named inside it exists.
- Do not turn a user hypothesis into a source and then cite it back to the user as independent corroboration.
- Do not infer mental-health state, vulnerability, motive, or threat state simply because the narrative makes it feel coherent.
- Agreement with the user is not evidence.
- Disagreement with the user is not evidence either.
- Preserve the user's actual proposition exactly before adjudicating it.
- When the evidence stops, **the conclusion stops**.

And I would add one particularly nasty Judge check:

> **PROVENANCE LOOP DETECTION:** Has any claim become “verified” only because an earlier model generated a document asserting it?

Because holy shit, this transcript contains textbook provenance laundering. The research pass explicitly says the dossiers indicate a systematic monitoring program, even though its evidentiary bridge is the dossier's own generated language. fileciteturn156file0L443-L475

That makes this much more useful than a sterile hallucination benchmark. It's a **long-context example of the model being pulled progressively into a shared narrative until it stops distinguishing evidence from inference**.

For the OMP architecture, I'd use the raw file as immutable evidence and derive a small Judge rubric from it. I would **not** dump all 696 lines into the Judge's permanent system prompt, because then you're risking teaching the Judge the same narrative associations you're asking it to detect.

So: **yes to the Judge. Strong yes. Just as prosecution exhibits, not scripture.**

[1348] assistant (text, 1727 chars)
Yep. **You were right. Context7 confirms OMP already has a first-class Judge slot.** So scratch my “add a Judge lane” language — we do **not** need to build one.

OMP already exposes:

```yaml
modelRoles:
  judge: <model>
```

and its `judge(state, questions)` evaluator resolves directly through that configured Judge backend. The built-in Judge candidate chain is currently:

```text
typesafe/jev-latest
openrouter/~typesafe/jev-latest
tiny
smol
default
active-session model
```

And this suddenly makes that earlier OMP output much more useful: it literally reported `judged 0` and `every judge candidate failed: openrouter/~typesafe/jev-latest rejected the account recently`. fileciteturn163file4L1316-L1348

So the job is much fucking simpler:

**configure the existing `modelRoles.judge` correctly → verify the provider/model actually answers → give that Judge the evidence/rubric/context we want it adjudicating.**

No new subsystem. No architectural surgery. No pretending OMP needs functionality it already fucking has.

Also useful: OMP supports explicit Judge fallback configuration under:

```yaml
retry:
  fallbackChains:
    judge:
      - ...
```

and TypeSafe's `jev-latest` / `jev-preview` are native Judge candidates when the account exposes them. OMP's docs specifically describe the Judge role as servicing typed judgments for things including the `judge()` eval helper, automatic thinking-level decisions, unexpected-stop detection, and AI staging decisions.

So once `gmri-mac.local` comes back, the correct first move is **inspect the actual current OMP config and credentials, find why the existing Judge chain failed, and bind the Judge we want.**

Much cleaner. And considerably less fucking work.

bash -lc cat > /mnt/data/build_gmri_production_packet.py <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import os, json, hashlib, shutil, zipfile, textwrap, stat, re

OUT = Path('/mnt/data/GMRI_PRODUCTION_DEPLOYMENT_DROP_2026-10-07')
SRC = Path('/mnt/data/gmri_prod_sources')
if OUT.exists():
    shutil.rmtree(OUT)
OUT.mkdir(parents=True)

provenance = {}

def write(rel, content, executable=False, origin='generated_clean_room'):
    p = OUT / rel
    p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    data = textwrap.dedent(content).lstrip('\n')
    p.write_text(data, encoding='utf-8')
    if executable:
        p.chmod(p.stat().st_mode | stat.S_IXUSR | stat.S_IXGRP | stat.S_IXOTH)
    provenance[str(rel)] = {'origin': origin}
    return p

def write_json(rel, obj, executable=False, origin='generated_clean_room'):
    return write(rel, json.dumps(obj, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + '\n', executable=executable, origin=origin)

def sha256(path):
    h=hashlib.sha256()
    with open(path,'rb') as f:
        for b in iter(lambda:f.read(1024*1024), b''):
            h.update(b)
    return h.hexdigest()

This is a **logical production topology**. Live discovery resolves existing resources, IDs, addresses, bridges, storage and capacity before mutation.

## Sovereign service plane
Prefer existing canonical GMRI resources when they satisfy the production service standard. If no suitable canonical resources exist, the resource resolver provisions the minimum isolated resources necessary for the deadline:

- **gmri-core**: GrizOS control plane, canonical durable mission/evidence/identity/authority state, Dottie runtime, AEGIS dispatch/runtime, memory/context adapter(s), model-routing adapter, health/observability and recovery services.
- **gmri-gev**: existing God's Eye View application plus narrow GrizOS projection gateway. GEV remains read/projection-side relative to canonical GrizOS state.

A service may remain on a previously deployed canonical host if live inspection establishes that doing so is safer and preserves the constitution. The decision is written to `RESOURCE_BLUEPRINT.md` and the run evidence.

## Operator/engineering plane
MacBook / primary local OMP: coordination, OpenRig workers, worktrees, Apple builds and secure operator access. It is not automatically canonical state and the field runtime must continue if OMP/OpenRig exits.

## Apple/field plane
Discover existing macOS/iPadOS/iOS code first. The PRD requires real local Apple capability, voice-first interaction, intent-first/generated UI, spatial state and meaningful offline behavior. Existing product surfaces are built/deployed; they are not replaced by a CLI merely because a CLI is easier to automate.

## External/provider plane
External model/data providers remain replaceable dependencies with explicit source/freshness/degraded state. Provider loss cannot silently rewrite canonical state or identity.
''')

write('RESOURCE_BLUEPRINT.md', r'''
# Resource Blueprint

`proxmox/resource_blueprint/desired_resources.json` defines the minimum logical resources. `resolve_blueprint.py` combines it with a normalized observer inventory and emits the concrete collision-free resource blueprint into the active run's evidence directory.

The resolver never invents a live network, storage pool, VM/LXC ID or capacity. If the observer inventory is incomplete, it returns `BLOCKED_REQUIRES_OPERATOR` for that resource rather than guessing.

Existing resources are adopted only after they are classified as canonical/appropriate and pass required health/state checks. New resources require rollback/snapshot/backup references before mutation.
''')

write('SECURITY_AUTHORITY.md', r'''
# Security and Authority

Default unattended authority: `OBSERVE`, `RETRIEVE`, `COMPARE`, `REASON`, `INVESTIGATE`, `COLLECT_EVIDENCE`, `REPORT`, `ALERT`.

Mutation requires prior authority appropriate to the target and must be bounded, reversible and idempotent. Never self-grant authority; broaden Proxmox privileges; disable TLS verification; expose arbitrary public ports; invent credentials; write secrets to Git/chat/evidence; delete evidence; overwrite known-good resources without rollback; or allow a framework to rewrite identity/memory policy.

Secrets are injected through operator-controlled secret files/stores or existing environment mechanisms. Packet templates contain names/references only.

Every consequential action records actor, authority, target, intended effect, observed pre-state, command/tool receipt, observed result, independent verification and rollback reference.
''')

write('MEMORY_POLICY.md', r'''
# Memory Policy

Canonical identity and policy belong to GrizOS/GMRI, not to a convenience framework.

If OpenViking is selected after version/licensing/live-fit verification, Dottie and every AEGIS intelligence use separate tenant/user boundaries. Private memory is private by default. Shared resources require explicit principal, peer and purpose; the share is an attributable event. Automatic autobiographical promotion, silent durable extraction and autonomous self-evolution are disabled. Durable promotion requires source/owner/authority validation plus receipt.

Existing GMRI memory systems (including HoloGraph or current production memory fabric) are candidates to integrate, not assumptions. OMP must inspect their current code, provenance semantics, persistence/recovery and compatibility with the GrizOS constitution before selecting them.
''')

write('EVIDENCE_PROVENANCE.md', r'''
# Evidence and Provenance

Preserve: `SOURCE TEXT → SOURCE CLAIM → OUR INTERPRETATION → GRAPH RELATION → DERIVED STATE`.

Evidence is not truth; vector similarity is not evidence; model output is not a source claim; a graph edge without provenance is not evidence.

Production evidence records carry source identity, retrieval/observation time, content hash where available, source class, transformations, actor, confidence/evidence state, and links to the mission/finding that used it. Contradictions stay attributed rather than being cosmetically reconciled.
''')

write('FIELD_MISSION_SET.md', r'''
# Friday–Saturday Field Mission Set

The field runtime performs real bounded GMRI work. OMP must reconcile this baseline set with current active work before field start and bind each mission to a real source/capability adapter.

1. **Production infrastructure watch** — observe GrizOS/Dottie/AEGIS/GEV service health, restart/reconciliation events, storage pressure, provider degradation and authority denials. Alert only on material consequence.
2. **GEV / spatial-source watch** — monitor the deployed GEV service and selected real source freshness/provider errors. Preserve source attribution and distinguish stale/fallback/simulated data from official/observed data.
3. **Active GMRI repository watch** — compare selected canonical repository heads/CI state against the field-start baseline (including the active GrizOS/Apple/GEV repos discovered at deployment). Report material changes; do not auto-merge or mutate repositories.
4. **Research/evidence watch** — process only the real authorized research/evidence inbox selected during deployment; collect/corroborate/source material, preserve contradictions and receipts, and never promote model interpretation to primary evidence.
5. **Recovery watch** — detect service/provider failure, attempt only preauthorized reversible recovery, reconcile uncertain effects before retry, and leave operator decisions queued rather than inventing authority.

The exact mission definitions are materialized into the deployed GrizOS mission interface by `operations/field_start.py` from `field/mission-set.json` after OMP binds real adapters/commands. No local counter, fixture or fake feed satisfies a mission.
''')

write('FIELD_OPERATIONS.md', r'''
# Field Operations

`operations/field_start.py`, `field_status.py`, and `field_stop.py` use the production deployment lock and the real GrizOS mission submit/status commands recorded by OMP. They refuse commands that reference fixture/mock/counter/testdata paths.

Field start records a baseline of service health, identity/state hashes, selected repository heads, provider status and active authority leases. Field status reports missions started/completed/failed/blocked, findings, evidence, authority denials, unauthorized mutations, memory leakage events, reconciliations, service/provider recoveries and operator interventions. Field stop requests a clean bounded stop through the real mission interface and preserves the final receipt.

write('RECOVERY.md', r'''
# Recovery

Recovery is reconcile-first, not retry-first.

1. Read durable run and production state.
2. Inspect actual process/service/storage/provider state.
3. Compare intended effect with observed effect.
4. Identify in-flight/uncertain operations and idempotency keys.
5. Reconcile canonical state and preserve both sides of conflicts.
6. Only then retry or resume.

Never blindly redispatch an interrupted consequential mutation. Identity/state/evidence must survive worker replacement, process kill and host/container restart. `acceptance/restart_recovery.py` verifies this against live services using the lock-defined state paths and commands.
''')

write('ROLLBACK.md', r'''
# Rollback

Rollback is established before each infrastructure or release mutation.

- Proxmox: snapshot/backup or equivalent known-good recovery reference before changing existing canonical resources; new resources have explicit delete/disable path after evidence preservation.
- Application release: immutable commit-addressed release directories with an atomic `current` symlink; rollback changes the symlink to the previous verified release and restarts the service.
- Database/schema: run only migrations that identify a backup/export and a tested reverse/restore path; never infer reversibility.
- Identity/memory: never roll back by deleting history. Restore known-good state while preserving conflict/audit evidence and lineage.

Use `proxmox/rollback/rollback_release.sh` and the component's recorded rollback command. Validate restored health independently.
''')

write('ACCEPTANCE.md', r'''
# Production Acceptance

A code file or green unit test is not production acceptance. The live deployed system must demonstrate, with receipts:

1. actual GrizOS production services running on the selected substrate;
2. canonical state persistence across service and host/container restart as applicable;
3. persistent Dottie identity with real model binding;
4. at least one persistent AEGIS identity with private memory, then two-member attributed interaction;
5. Dottie dispatch of a real mission through the GrizOS authority/capability boundary;
6. actual inference by the deployed provider/model, not a fixture;
7. observation of a real approved evidence/research/system source;
8. durable finding/event/evidence with provenance;
9. actual GEV projection of canonical world-state events without GEV becoming canonical;
10. actual denial of an out-of-envelope authority request;
11. duplicate dispatch does not duplicate a consequential effect;
12. worker/process kill mid-mission followed by reconciliation without blind duplicate effect;
13. deployed private-memory cross-access denied; explicit sharing attributed/receipted;
14. provider/WAN loss produces truthful degraded behavior and meaningful local capability to the implemented extent;
15. backup/snapshot plus one safe restore/recovery exercise;
16. independent Proxmox observer agrees with intended state or records exact discrepancy;
17. remote status can be checked without turning the operator into the implementation engine;
18. field missions continue when interactive OMP/OpenRig is closed.

`acceptance/production_acceptance.py` is evidence aggregation and gate logic; it does not manufacture product behavior. Live acceptance commands come from source-derived component locks and are rejected if they point at fixture/mock/counter/testdata artifacts.
''')

Seeded high-consequence modes to exercise: process kill mid-mission; acknowledgement lost after effect; duplicate dispatch; restart with uncertain state; stale/contradictory evidence; provider/tool outage; unauthorized authority escalation; private-memory cross-read; unauthorized memory promotion; GEV disconnect/staleness; malformed capability; failed release followed by known-good rollback; Apple endpoint disconnect; WAN loss.

write('bootstrap/clean_room_guard.py', r'''#!/usr/bin/env python3
import argparse, os, sys
from pathlib import Path
DENY = ('GMRI_OVERNIGHT_DROP', 'gmri-overnight-integration-plan.md')
p=argparse.ArgumentParser(); p.add_argument('--packet-root',required=True); p.add_argument('--path',action='append',default=[]); a=p.parse_args()
root=Path(a.packet_root).resolve()
viol=[]
for raw in [str(root), *a.path]:
    s=str(Path(raw).expanduser())
    if any(x.lower() in s.lower() for x in DENY): viol.append(s)
# Packet contents may mention prohibited names in policy text, but no symlink/import may point to them.
for f in root.rglob('*'):
    if f.is_symlink():
        t=str(f.resolve())
        if any(x.lower() in t.lower() for x in DENY): viol.append(f'{f} -> {t}')
if viol:
    print('CLEAN_ROOM_FAIL')
    for v in viol: print(v)
    sys.exit(2)
print('CLEAN_ROOM_PASS')
''', executable=True)

write('bootstrap/initialize_run_state.py', r'''#!/usr/bin/env python3
import argparse, json, os, secrets
from pathlib import Path
from datetime import datetime, timezone
p=argparse.ArgumentParser(); p.add_argument('--runs-root',required=True); a=p.parse_args()
root=Path(a.runs_root).resolve(); root.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
now=datetime.now(timezone.utc); rid='prod-'+now.strftime('%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ')+'-'+secrets.token_hex(4)
r=root/rid; (r/'EVIDENCE').mkdir(parents=True)
def dump(n,o): (r/n).write_text(json.dumps(o,indent=2,sort_keys=True)+'\n')
dump('MISSION.json',{'run_id':rid,'mission':'GMRI production deployment','created_at':now.isoformat(),'hard_gate':'2026-10-08T23:59:00 local','status':'DISCOVERY'})
dump('STATE.json',{'run_id':rid,'state':'DISCOVERY','last_reconciled_at':None,'component_locks':{},'in_flight':[]})
(r/'CHECKPOINT.md').write_text('# Checkpoint\n\nDiscovery initialized. No production mutation recorded yet.\n')
(r/'EVENTS.jsonl').write_text(json.dumps({'event':'RUN_CREATED','at':now.isoformat(),'run_id':rid})+'\n')
(r/'COMMANDS.jsonl').write_text('')
dump('ACCEPTANCE.json',{'overall':'NOT_RUN','gates':{}})
dump('RECOVERY.json',{'sequence':['READ_DURABLE_STATE','INSPECT_REALITY','COMPARE','RECONCILE','CONTINUE'],'rollback_refs':[]})
packet=Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]; (packet/'.current_run').write_text(str(r)+'\n')
print(r)
''', executable=True)

write('bootstrap/preflight.sh', r'''#!/bin/sh
set -u
ROOT=$(CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname -- "$0")/.." && pwd)
RUN=$(cat "$ROOT/.current_run" 2>/dev/null || true)
if [ -z "$RUN" ] || [ ! -d "$RUN" ]; then echo "run state missing; run initialize_run_state.py" >&2; exit 2; fi
OUT="$RUN/EVIDENCE/preflight.txt"
: > "$OUT"
log(){ printf '%s\n' "$*" | tee -a "$OUT"; }
log "GMRI production preflight"
log "utc=$(date -u '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ')"
log "host=$(hostname 2>/dev/null || true)"
log "pwd=$PWD"
for c in python3 git gh node npm omp openrig ollama ssh rsync jq curl docker podman xcodebuild swift; do
  if command -v "$c" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    log "FOUND $c=$(command -v "$c")"
    case "$c" in
      omp|openrig|ollama|python3|git|gh|node|npm|docker|podman|swift) "$c" --version >> "$OUT" 2>&1 || true ;;
      xcodebuild) xcodebuild -version >> "$OUT" 2>&1 || true ;;
    esac
  else
    log "MISSING $c"
  fi
done
if command -v omp >/dev/null 2>&1; then { echo '--- omp --help ---'; omp --help; } >> "$OUT" 2>&1 || true; fi
if command -v openrig >/dev/null 2>&1; then { echo '--- openrig --help ---'; openrig --help; } >> "$OUT" 2>&1 || true; fi
if command -v ollama >/dev/null 2>&1; then { echo '--- ollama list ---'; ollama list; } >> "$OUT" 2>&1 || true; fi
printf '%s\n' "$OUT"
''', executable=True)

write('bootstrap/discover_versions.sh', r'''#!/bin/sh
set -u
OUT=${1:?output path required}
mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"; : > "$OUT"
for c in python3 git gh node npm omp openrig ollama docker podman xcodebuild swift; do
  if command -v "$c" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    printf '## %s\n' "$c" >> "$OUT"
    case "$c" in xcodebuild) xcodebuild -version >> "$OUT" 2>&1 || true;; *) "$c" --version >> "$OUT" 2>&1 || true;; esac
  fi
done
''', executable=True)

write('bootstrap/discover_repos.py', r'''#!/usr/bin/env python3
import argparse,json,subprocess,os
from pathlib import Path
p=argparse.ArgumentParser(); p.add_argument('--out',required=True); p.add_argument('--roots',nargs='*'); a=p.parse_args()
roots=[Path(x).expanduser() for x in (a.roots or ['~/Desktop','~/Documents','~/Projects','~/src','~/research'])]
deny=('GMRI_OVERNIGHT_DROP','gmri-overnight-integration-plan.md')
seen=[]
for root in roots:
    if not root.exists(): continue
    for gd in root.rglob('.git'):
        repo=gd.parent.resolve(); s=str(repo)
        if any(d.lower() in s.lower() for d in deny): continue
        try:
            def run(*args): return subprocess.check_output(args,cwd=repo,text=True,stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL).strip()
            seen.append({'path':s,'head':run('git','rev-parse','HEAD'),'branch':run('git','branch','--show-current'),'origin':run('git','remote','get-url','origin'),'status':run('git','status','--short')})
        except Exception as e: seen.append({'path':s,'error':str(e)})
out=Path(a.out); out.parent.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True); out.write_text(json.dumps({'local_repositories':seen},indent=2,sort_keys=True)+'\n')
print(out)
''', executable=True)

import argparse,json,shlex,subprocess,sys

write('bootstrap/scan_secrets.py', r'''#!/usr/bin/env python3
import argparse,re,sys
from pathlib import Path
p=argparse.ArgumentParser(); p.add_argument('root'); a=p.parse_args(); root=Path(a.root)
# Deliberately conservative; templates/placeholders allowed.
patterns=[
 ('private_key',re.compile(r'-----BEGIN (?:RSA |EC |OPENSSH )?PRIVATE KEY-----')),
 ('github_token',re.compile(r'gh[pousr]_[A-Za-z0-9]{30,}')),
 ('aws_key',re.compile(r'AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}')),
 ('bearer_literal',re.compile(r'(?i)authorization\s*[:=]\s*bearer\s+[A-Za-z0-9._-]{20,}')),
]
findings=[]
for f in root.rglob('*'):
    if not f.is_file() or f.name=='MANIFEST.sha256': continue
    try: s=f.read_text(errors='ignore')
    except: continue
    for name,rx in patterns:
        if rx.search(s): findings.append((str(f.relative_to(root)),name))
if findings:
    for x in findings: print('SECRET_PATTERN',*x)
    sys.exit(2)
print('SECRET_SCAN_PASS')
''', executable=True)

write('bootstrap/validate_packet.py', r'''#!/usr/bin/env python3
import argparse,json,os,re,subprocess,sys
from pathlib import Path
p=argparse.ArgumentParser(); p.add_argument('root'); a=p.parse_args(); root=Path(a.root).resolve()
required=['START_HERE.md','PRODUCTION_MISSION.md','SOURCE_AUTHORITY.md','CLEAN_ROOM_ATTESTATION.md','LIVE_DISCOVERY.md','ARCHITECTURE_CONSTITUTION.md','PRODUCTION_TOPOLOGY.md','RESOURCE_BLUEPRINT.md','SECURITY_AUTHORITY.md','MODEL_ROUTING.md','MEMORY_POLICY.md','EVIDENCE_PROVENANCE.md','FIELD_MISSION_SET.md','FIELD_OPERATIONS.md','RECOVERY.md','ROLLBACK.md','ACCEPTANCE.md','FAILURE_MODE_REGISTER.md','MORNING_HANDOFF.md','.omp/AGENTS.md','.omp/RULES.md','bootstrap/preflight.sh','bootstrap/discover_repos.py','proxmox/resource_blueprint/resolve_blueprint.py','operations/field_start.py','acceptance/production_acceptance.py']
err=[]
for r in required:
    f=root/r
    if not f.exists() or (f.is_file() and f.stat().st_size<40): err.append('missing/substantive '+r)
# No symlink or source-material path may point into prohibited generated packet/plan.
for f in root.rglob('*'):
    if f.is_symlink():
        t=str(f.resolve()).lower()
        if 'gmri_overnight_drop' in t or 'gmri-overnight-integration-plan.md' in t: err.append('prohibited symlink '+str(f))
# Executable acceptance code must reject synthetic substitutes.
acc=(root/'acceptance/production_acceptance.py').read_text()
for term in ['fixture','mock','counter','testdata']:
    if term not in acc.lower(): err.append('acceptance missing synthetic guard '+term)
# Proxmox may not be silently deferred.
start=(root/'START_HERE.md').read_text().lower(); topo=(root/'PRODUCTION_TOPOLOGY.md').read_text().lower()
if 'operator lane' not in start or 'observer lane' not in start: err.append('two-lane proxmox missing')
if 'gmri-core' not in topo or 'gmri-gev' not in topo: err.append('logical production resources missing')
# Validate JSON files.
for f in root.rglob('*.json'):
    try: json.loads(f.read_text())
    except Exception as e: err.append(f'json {f.relative_to(root)}: {e}')
# Parse python and shell syntax.
for f in root.rglob('*.py'):
    r=subprocess.run([sys.executable,'-m','py_compile',str(f)],capture_output=True,text=True)
    if r.returncode: err.append(f'python syntax {f.relative_to(root)}: {r.stderr.strip()}')
for f in root.rglob('*.sh'):
    r=subprocess.run(['bash','-n',str(f)],capture_output=True,text=True)
    if r.returncode: err.append(f'shell syntax {f.relative_to(root)}: {r.stderr.strip()}')
if err:
    print('PACKET_VALIDATION_FAIL')
    for e in err: print('-',e)
    sys.exit(2)
print('PACKET_VALIDATION_PASS')
print('files='+str(sum(1 for f in root.rglob('*') if f.is_file())))
''', executable=True)

write('proxmox/resource_blueprint/resolve_blueprint.py', r'''#!/usr/bin/env python3
import argparse,json,sys
from pathlib import Path
p=argparse.ArgumentParser(); p.add_argument('--inventory',required=True); p.add_argument('--desired',default=str(Path(__file__).with_name('desired_resources.json'))); p.add_argument('--out',required=True); a=p.parse_args()
inv=json.loads(Path(a.inventory).read_text()); des=json.loads(Path(a.desired).read_text())
if not inv.get('nodes') or not inv.get('storages') or not inv.get('networks'):
    raise SystemExit('BLOCKED_REQUIRES_OPERATOR: observer inventory lacks node/storage/network data')
used=set()
for g in inv.get('guests',[]):
    for k in ('vmid','id'):
        try: used.add(int(g[k])); break
        except: pass
nextid=100
while nextid in used: nextid+=1
# Storage choice must be explicit from observer attributes; prefer content that advertises rootdir/images and sufficient free GB.
def storage_for(kind):
    candidates=[]
    for s in inv['storages']:
        content=str(s.get('content',''))
        if ('rootdir' in content or 'images' in content) and s.get('active',True): candidates.append(s)
    if not candidates: raise SystemExit('BLOCKED_REQUIRES_OPERATOR: no active VM/LXC-capable storage observed')
    candidates.sort(key=lambda x: float(x.get('avail_gb',x.get('free_gb',0)) or 0), reverse=True)
    return candidates[0].get('storage') or candidates[0].get('name')
network=inv['networks'][0].get('bridge') or inv['networks'][0].get('name')
if not network: raise SystemExit('BLOCKED_REQUIRES_OPERATOR: network bridge/name absent from normalized inventory')
node=inv['nodes'][0].get('node') or inv['nodes'][0].get('name')
if not node: raise SystemExit('BLOCKED_REQUIRES_OPERATOR: node name absent')
resolved=[]
for r in des['resources']:
    existing=next((g for g in inv.get('guests',[]) if g.get('name')==r['logical_name'] and g.get('gmri_canonical') is True),None)
    if existing:
        resolved.append({'logical_name':r['logical_name'],'action':'ADOPT_VERIFY','existing':existing,'node':existing.get('node',node)})
    else:
        while nextid in used: nextid+=1
        resolved.append({'logical_name':r['logical_name'],'action':'CREATE','vmid':nextid,'node':node,'storage':storage_for(r['kind']),'bridge':network,'minimum':r['minimum'],'network_policy':r['network']})
        used.add(nextid); nextid+=1
out={'source_inventory':a.inventory,'resolved':resolved,'status':'PROPOSED_FROM_OBSERVED_INVENTORY_REQUIRES_OPERATOR_LANE_EXECUTION'}
Path(a.out).write_text(json.dumps(out,indent=2,sort_keys=True)+'\n'); print(a.out)
''', executable=True)

write('proxmox/deploy/guest_apply.py', r'''#!/usr/bin/env python3
# Production release installer. Run as root inside the selected production guest.
import argparse,json,os,shlex,subprocess,sys,tempfile,hashlib
from pathlib import Path
p=argparse.ArgumentParser(); p.add_argument('--lock',required=True); p.add_argument('--staged-source'); p.add_argument('--env-file'); a=p.parse_args()
if os.geteuid()!=0: raise SystemExit('root required')
lock=json.loads(Path(a.lock).read_text()); name=lock['name']; commit=lock['commit']; base=Path('/opt/gmri/releases')/name; rel=base/commit; base.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
if not rel.exists():
    src=lock['source']; kind=src['kind']
    if kind=='git':
        url=src['url']; subprocess.run(['git','clone','--no-checkout',url,str(rel)],check=True); subprocess.run(['git','checkout','--detach',commit],cwd=rel,check=True)
    elif kind in ('local_git','staged_release'):
        if not a.staged_source: raise SystemExit('staged source required for '+kind)
        s=Path(a.staged_source).resolve(); subprocess.run(['rsync','-a','--delete',str(s)+'/ ',str(rel)+'/'],shell=True,check=False)
        # Avoid shell ambiguity above by fallback Python copy only if rsync invocation failed.
        if not rel.exists() or not any(rel.iterdir()):
            import shutil; shutil.copytree(s,rel,dirs_exist_ok=True)
    else: raise SystemExit('unsupported source kind')
# Verify commit when source is a git checkout.
if (rel/'.git').exists():
    head=subprocess.check_output(['git','rev-parse','HEAD'],cwd=rel,text=True).strip()
    if head!=commit: raise SystemExit('release commit mismatch')
# Build exactly source-derived argv.
if lock.get('build_cmd'): subprocess.run(lock['build_cmd'],cwd=rel,check=True)
# Atomically select release.
cur=base/'current'; tmp=base/'.current.new'
try: tmp.unlink()
except FileNotFoundError: pass
tmp.symlink_to(rel.name); os.replace(tmp,cur)
# Environment ref is installed owner-only if explicitly supplied by operator.
if a.env_file:
    envsrc=Path(a.env_file); envdst=Path('/etc/gmri')/(name+'.env')
    envdst.write_bytes(envsrc.read_bytes()); envdst.chmod(0o600)
print(json.dumps({'component':name,'commit':commit,'release':str(rel),'current':str(cur)}))

write('spatial-gev/config/projection-gateway.env.example', r'''

GRIZOS_EVENTS_URL=http://REPLACE_INTERNAL_GRIZOS/events
GEV_GATEWAY_BIND=127.0.0.1
GEV_GATEWAY_PORT=8766
GEV_STALE_AFTER_SECONDS=60

write('spatial-gev/adapters/grizos_projection_gateway.py', r'''#!/usr/bin/env python3
# Narrow read-only projection gateway derived from the GMRI spatial architecture.
# It never writes canonical state. On upstream failure it serves last-known-good with explicit stale/degraded metadata.
import json,os,time,urllib.request,threading
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler,ThreadingHTTPServer
SNAP=os.environ['GRIZOS_SNAPSHOT_URL']; EVENTS=os.environ['GRIZOS_EVENTS_URL']; BIND=os.getenv('GEV_GATEWAY_BIND','127.0.0.1'); PORT=int(os.getenv('GEV_GATEWAY_PORT','8766')); STALE=int(os.getenv('GEV_STALE_AFTER_SECONDS','60'))
cache={'snapshot':None,'events':None,'snapshot_at':0.0,'events_at':0.0,'errors':{}}
def fetch(k,url):
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(url,timeout=5) as r: data=json.load(r)
        cache[k]=data; cache[k+'_at']=time.time(); cache['errors'].pop(k,None)
    except Exception as e: cache['errors'][k]=str(e)
def loop():
    while True:
        fetch('snapshot',SNAP); fetch('events',EVENTS); time.sleep(5)
class H(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def sendj(self,o,status=200):
        b=json.dumps(o).encode(); self.send_response(status); self.send_header('Content-Type','application/json'); self.send_header('Content-Length',str(len(b))); self.end_headers(); self.wfile.write(b)
    def do_GET(self):
        now=time.time()
        if self.path=='/health': return self.sendj({'ok':cache['snapshot'] is not None,'projection_only':True,'upstream_errors':cache['errors'],'snapshot_age_s':None if not cache['snapshot_at'] else round(now-cache['snapshot_at'],2)})
        if self.path=='/snapshot': return self.sendj({'canonical':False,'projection_only':True,'stale':not cache['snapshot_at'] or now-cache['snapshot_at']>STALE,'observed_at':cache['snapshot_at'],'upstream':SNAP,'data':cache['snapshot'],'error':cache['errors'].get('snapshot')},200 if cache['snapshot'] is not None else 503)
        if self.path=='/events': return self.sendj({'canonical':False,'projection_only':True,'stale':not cache['events_at'] or now-cache['events_at']>STALE,'observed_at':cache['events_at'],'upstream':EVENTS,'data':cache['events'],'error':cache['errors'].get('events')},200 if cache['events'] is not None else 503)
        self.sendj({'error':'not found'},404)
    def log_message(self,fmt,*args): return
threading.Thread(target=loop,daemon=True).start(); ThreadingHTTPServer((BIND,PORT),H).serve_forever()
''', executable=True)
write('spatial-gev/deploy/deploy_gev.sh', r'''#!/bin/sh

# Upstream package currently defines doctor/build; verify package before use.
node -e 'let p=require("./package.json"); if(!p.scripts||!p.scripts.build) process.exit(2); console.log(p.version,p.engines||{})'
npm ci
if npm run | grep -q 'doctor'; then npm run doctor; fi
npm run build
''', executable=True)

write('operations/_lib.py', r'''import json,subprocess,re,hashlib,os
from pathlib import Path
BANNED=('fixture','mock','counter','testdata')
def load(path): return json.loads(Path(path).read_text())
def safe_cmd(cmd):
    if not isinstance(cmd,list) or not cmd or not all(isinstance(x,str) for x in cmd): raise ValueError('command must be nonempty argv list')
    s=' '.join(cmd).lower()
    if any(x in s for x in BANNED): raise ValueError('synthetic substitute forbidden in field/production command: '+s)
    return cmd
def run(cmd,**kw): return subprocess.run(safe_cmd(cmd),**kw)
def sha_path(p):
    h=hashlib.sha256(); f=Path(p)
    if f.is_file(): h.update(f.read_bytes()); return h.hexdigest()
    for x in sorted(q for q in f.rglob('*') if q.is_file()): h.update(str(x.relative_to(f)).encode()); h.update(x.read_bytes())
    return h.hexdigest()
''')

# ---------------- acceptance ----------------
write('acceptance/_live.py', r'''import json,subprocess,re,hashlib,time,os
from pathlib import Path
BANNED=('fixture','mock','counter','testdata')
def load(p): return json.loads(Path(p).read_text())
def cmd_ok(cmd):
    if not isinstance(cmd,list) or not cmd: raise ValueError('missing live argv command')
    s=' '.join(cmd).lower()
    if any(x in s for x in BANNED): raise ValueError('synthetic acceptance command forbidden: '+s)
    return cmd
def run(cmd):
    q=subprocess.run(cmd_ok(cmd),capture_output=True,text=True); return {'exit':q.returncode,'output':(q.stdout+q.stderr)[-12000:]}
def hash_path(p):
    p=Path(p); h=hashlib.sha256()
    if p.is_file(): h.update(p.read_bytes())
    elif p.is_dir():
        for f in sorted(x for x in p.rglob('*') if x.is_file()): h.update(str(f.relative_to(p)).encode()); h.update(f.read_bytes())
    else: return None
    return h.hexdigest()
''')
write('acceptance/production_acceptance.py', r'''#!/usr/bin/env python3
import argparse,json,sys,time
from pathlib import Path
sys.path.insert(0,str(Path(__file__).parent)); from _live import load,run,cmd_ok
p=argparse.ArgumentParser(); p.add_argument('--deployment-lock',required=True); p.add_argument('--out',required=True); a=p.parse_args(); d=load(a.deployment_lock); gates={}
# Synthetic-substitute words are deliberately guarded: fixture, mock, counter, testdata.
required_live=['real_inference','real_dispatch','real_evidence','authority_denial','memory_isolation','reconcile','gev_projection','backup_restore','field_runtime_independent']
for name,c in d.get('components',{}).items(): gates['health:'+name]=run(c['health_cmd'])
ac=d.get('acceptance_commands',{})
for key in required_live:
    if key not in ac: gates[key]={'exit':99,'output':'NOT_CONFIGURED_FROM_REAL_IMPLEMENTATION'}
    else: gates[key]=run(ac[key])
# Gate cannot be made ready by tests alone: every named live command must execute successfully.
passed=all(x['exit']==0 for x in gates.values())
overall='LIVE_ACCEPTANCE_PASS' if passed else 'LIVE_ACCEPTANCE_NOT_PASSED'
obj={'at':time.time(),'overall':overall,'gates':gates,'tests_are_not_product_acceptance':True}; Path(a.out).write_text(json.dumps(obj,indent=2,sort_keys=True)+'\n'); print(overall); raise SystemExit(0 if passed else 2)
''', executable=True)
write('acceptance/restart_recovery.py', r'''#!/usr/bin/env python3
import argparse,json,subprocess,sys,time
from pathlib import Path
sys.path.insert(0,str(Path(__file__).parent)); from _live import load,run,hash_path
p=argparse.ArgumentParser(); p.add_argument('--deployment-lock',required=True); p.add_argument('--component',required=True); p.add_argument('--out',required=True); a=p.parse_args(); d=load(a.deployment_lock); c=d['components'][a.component]
before={p:hash_path(p) for p in c['persistent_state_paths']}; pre=run(c['health_cmd'])
# Restart through production supervisor when recorded, otherwise stop/start source-derived commands.
if c.get('systemd_service'): subprocess.run(['systemctl','restart',c['systemd_service']],check=True)
else: run(c['stop_cmd']); run(c['start_cmd'])
after={p:hash_path(p) for p in c['persistent_state_paths']}; post=run(c['health_cmd']); rec={'before_hashes':before,'after_hashes':after,'pre_health':pre,'post_health':post,'identity_state_paths_persisted':all(v is not None for v in after.values())}; Path(a.out).write_text(json.dumps(rec,indent=2)+'\n'); raise SystemExit(0 if post['exit']==0 and rec['identity_state_paths_persisted'] else 2)
''', executable=True)

from pathlib import Path
BANNED=('fixture','mock','counter','testdata')
def load(path): return json.loads(Path(path).read_text())
def safe_cmd(cmd):
    if not isinstance(cmd,list) or not cmd or not all(isinstance(x,str) for x in cmd): raise ValueError('command must be nonempty argv list')
    s=' '.join(cmd).lower()
    if any(x in s for x in BANNED): raise ValueError('synthetic substitute forbidden in field/production command: '+s)

def run(cmd,**kw): return subprocess.run(safe_cmd(cmd),**kw)
def sha_path(p):
    h=hashlib.sha256(); f=Path(p)
    if f.is_file(): h.update(f.read_bytes()); return h.hexdigest()
    for x in sorted(q for q in f.rglob('*') if q.is_file()): h.update(str(x.relative_to(f)).encode()); h.update(x.read_bytes())

def cmd_ok(cmd):
    if not isinstance(cmd,list) or not cmd: raise ValueError('missing live argv command')
    s=' '.join(cmd).lower()
    if any(x in s for x in BANNED): raise ValueError('synthetic acceptance command forbidden: '+s)

    q=subprocess.run(cmd_ok(cmd),capture_output=True,text=True); return {'exit':q.returncode,'output':(q.stdout+q.stderr)[-12000:]}
def hash_path(p):
    p=Path(p); h=hashlib.sha256()
    if p.is_file(): h.update(p.read_bytes())
    elif p.is_dir():
        for f in sorted(x for x in p.rglob('*') if x.is_file()): h.update(str(f.relative_to(p)).encode()); h.update(f.read_bytes())
    else: return None
    return h.hexdigest()
''')

w('bootstrap/run_command.py', '''
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import argparse, json, os, subprocess, time, uuid, hashlib
from pathlib import Path
p=argparse.ArgumentParser(); p.add_argument('--run-dir',required=True); p.add_argument('--actor',required=True); p.add_argument('--location',required=True); p.add_argument('--authority-ref'); p.add_argument('--rollback-ref'); p.add_argument('cmd',nargs=argparse.REMAINDER); a=p.parse_args()
if not a.cmd: raise SystemExit('command argv required after --')
if a.cmd[0]=='--': a.cmd=a.cmd[1:]
if not a.cmd: raise SystemExit('empty command')
run=Path(a.run_dir); ev=run/'EVIDENCE'/'commands'; ev.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
tok=time.strftime('%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ',time.gmtime())+'-'+uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]
out=ev/(tok+'.stdout'); err=ev/(tok+'.stderr'); started=time.time()
with out.open('wb') as so, err.open('wb') as se:
    q=subprocess.run(a.cmd,stdout=so,stderr=se)
def sh(path):
    h=hashlib.sha256(); h.update(path.read_bytes()); return h.hexdigest()
rec={'at':started,'actor':a.actor,'location':a.location,'authority_ref':a.authority_ref,'rollback_ref':a.rollback_ref,'argv':a.cmd,'exit_code':q.returncode,'stdout':str(out),'stdout_sha256':sh(out),'stderr':str(err),'stderr_sha256':sh(err),'duration_s':round(time.time()-started,3)}
with (run/'COMMANDS.jsonl').open('a') as f: f.write(json.dumps(rec,separators=(',',':'))+'\n')
print(json.dumps(rec)); raise SystemExit(q.returncode)
''', True)

# Replace release staging/install with exact-commit, no-shell mechanics.
w('proxmox/deploy/stage_component.sh', '''
#!/bin/sh
set -eu
SRC=${1:?source repo}; TARGET=${2:?ssh target}; DEST=${3:?guest staging dir}; COMMIT=${4:?exact commit}
[ -d "$SRC/.git" ] || { echo 'source is not a git checkout' >&2; exit 2; }
OBS=$(git -C "$SRC" rev-parse "$COMMIT^{commit}")
[ "$OBS" = "$COMMIT" ] || { echo 'commit did not resolve exactly' >&2; exit 2; }
ssh "$TARGET" "rm -rf '$DEST' && mkdir -p '$DEST'"
git -C "$SRC" archive --format=tar "$COMMIT" | ssh "$TARGET" "tar -xf - -C '$DEST' && printf '%s\\n' '$COMMIT' > '$DEST/.gmri-source-commit'"
''', True)

w('proxmox/deploy/guest_apply.py', '''
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import argparse,json,os,subprocess,shutil
from pathlib import Path
p=argparse.ArgumentParser(); p.add_argument('--lock',required=True); p.add_argument('--staged-source'); p.add_argument('--env-file'); a=p.parse_args()
if os.geteuid()!=0: raise SystemExit('root required')
lock=json.loads(Path(a.lock).read_text()); name=lock['name']; commit=lock['commit']; base=Path('/opt/gmri/releases')/name; rel=base/commit; base.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
if not rel.exists():
    src=lock['source']; kind=src['kind']
    if kind=='git':
        url=src['url']; subprocess.run(['git','clone','--no-checkout',url,str(rel)],check=True); subprocess.run(['git','checkout','--detach',commit],cwd=rel,check=True)
        head=subprocess.check_output(['git','rev-parse','HEAD'],cwd=rel,text=True).strip()
        if head!=commit: raise SystemExit('release commit mismatch')
    elif kind in ('local_git','staged_release'):
        if not a.staged_source: raise SystemExit('staged source required for '+kind)
        s=Path(a.staged_source).resolve(); marker=s/'.gmri-source-commit'
        if not marker.exists() or marker.read_text().strip()!=commit: raise SystemExit('staged source commit marker mismatch')
        shutil.copytree(s,rel,dirs_exist_ok=False)
    else: raise SystemExit('unsupported source kind')
if lock.get('build_cmd'): subprocess.run(lock['build_cmd'],cwd=rel,check=True)
cur=base/'current'; tmp=base/'.current.new'
try: tmp.unlink()
except FileNotFoundError: pass
tmp.symlink_to(rel.name); os.replace(tmp,cur)
if a.env_file:
    envsrc=Path(a.env_file); envdst=Path('/etc/gmri')/(name+'.env'); envdst.write_bytes(envsrc.read_bytes()); envdst.chmod(0o600)
print(json.dumps({'component':name,'commit':commit,'release':str(rel),'current':str(cur)}))
''', True)

w('proxmox/deploy/install_systemd_unit.sh', '''
#!/bin/sh
set -eu
UNIT=${1:?rendered unit}; WRAP=${2:?rendered start wrapper}; NAME=${3:?component name}
install -m 0755 "$WRAP" "/opt/gmri/bin/$NAME-start"
install -m 0644 "$UNIT" "/etc/systemd/system/gmri-$NAME.service"
systemctl daemon-reload
systemctl enable "gmri-$NAME.service"
systemctl restart "gmri-$NAME.service"
systemctl --no-pager --full status "gmri-$NAME.service"
''', True)

# Patch systemd renderer to include source-derived durable paths inside allowed writable set.
w('proxmox/deploy/render_systemd_unit.py', '''
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import argparse,json,shlex
from pathlib import Path
p=argparse.ArgumentParser(); p.add_argument('--lock',required=True); p.add_argument('--out',required=True); a=p.parse_args(); o=json.loads(Path(a.lock).read_text()); name=o['name']
q=lambda argv:' '.join(shlex.quote(x) for x in argv)
release=f'/opt/gmri/releases/{name}/current'; wrapper=f'/opt/gmri/bin/{name}-start'
paths=['/var/lib/gmri','/var/log/gmri',f'/opt/gmri/releases/{name}']+[x for x in o.get('persistent_state_paths',[]) if str(x).startswith('/')]
unit='''+'"""'+'''[Unit]
Description=GMRI {name}
After=network-online.target
Wants=network-online.target

[Service]
Type=simple
User={user}
Group={group}
WorkingDirectory={release}
EnvironmentFile=-/etc/gmri/{name}.env
ExecStart={wrapper}
Restart=on-failure
RestartSec=3
NoNewPrivileges=true
PrivateTmp=true
ProtectSystem=full
ReadWritePaths={rw}
TimeoutStopSec=30

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
'''+'"""'+'''.format(name=name,user=o['service_user'],group=o.get('service_group',o['service_user']),release=release,wrapper=wrapper,rw=' '.join(paths))
out=Path(a.out); out.parent.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True); out.write_text(unit)
wrap=out.with_suffix('.start.sh'); wrap.write_text('#!/bin/sh\\nset -eu\\ncd '+shlex.quote(release)+'\\nexec '+q(o['start_cmd'])+'\\n'); wrap.chmod(0o755)
print(out); print(wrap)
''', True)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
import argparse,json,sys,time
from pathlib import Path
p=argparse.ArgumentParser(); p.add_argument('--state-dir',required=True); p.add_argument('--existing'); p.add_argument('--lineage-version'); p.add_argument('--memory-namespace-ref'); p.add_argument('--relationship-state-ref'); p.add_argument('--model-binding'); a=p.parse_args()
out=Path(a.state_dir); out.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True); dest=out/'identity.json'
if dest.exists(): print(dest); sys.exit(0)
if a.existing:
    ex=Path(a.existing); obj=json.loads(ex.read_text())
else:
    need={'lineage-version':a.lineage_version,'memory-namespace-ref':a.memory_namespace_ref,'relationship-state-ref':a.relationship_state_ref,'model-binding':a.model_binding}; miss=[k for k,v in need.items() if not v]
    if miss: raise SystemExit('new identity requires '+','.join(miss))
    obj=json.loads((Path(__file__).parent/'manifest.template.json').read_text())
    obj['identity_manifest_ref']=str(dest); obj['lineage_version']=a.lineage_version; obj['memory_namespace_ref']=a.memory_namespace_ref; obj['relationship_state_ref']=a.relationship_state_ref
    obj['active_model_binding']={'model':a.model_binding,'bound_at':time.time()}; obj['model_binding_history']=[obj['active_model_binding']]
req=['intelligence_id','identity_manifest_ref','lineage_version','memory_namespace_ref','authority_profile_ref','relationship_state_ref','active_model_binding','model_binding_history']
for k in req:
    if k not in obj or obj[k] in (None,'') or (isinstance(obj[k],str) and obj[k].startswith('UNSET')): raise SystemExit('identity unresolved '+k)
dest.write_text(json.dumps(obj,indent=2,sort_keys=True)+'\n'); dest.chmod(0o600); print(dest)
''', True)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
import argparse,json,subprocess,sys,compileall
from pathlib import Path
p=argparse.ArgumentParser(); p.add_argument('root'); a=p.parse_args(); root=Path(a.root).resolve(); err=[]
required=['START_HERE.md','PRODUCTION_MISSION.md','SOURCE_AUTHORITY.md','CLEAN_ROOM_ATTESTATION.md','CONFLICT_REGISTER.md','LIVE_DISCOVERY.md','ARCHITECTURE_CONSTITUTION.md','PRODUCTION_TOPOLOGY.md','RESOURCE_BLUEPRINT.md','SECURITY_AUTHORITY.md','MODEL_ROUTING.md','MEMORY_POLICY.md','EVIDENCE_PROVENANCE.md','FIELD_MISSION_SET.md','FIELD_OPERATIONS.md','RECOVERY.md','ROLLBACK.md','ACCEPTANCE.md','FAILURE_MODE_REGISTER.md','MORNING_HANDOFF.md','.omp/AGENTS.md','.omp/RULES.md','bootstrap/preflight.sh','bootstrap/discover_repos.py','bootstrap/run_command.py','proxmox/resource_blueprint/resolve_blueprint.py','proxmox/deploy/guest_apply.py','proxmox/deploy/render_systemd_unit.py','proxmox/deploy/install_systemd_unit.sh','proxmox/backup/backup_guest_state.sh','proxmox/backup/restore_guest_state_to_staging.sh','dottie/identity/initialize_identity.py','aegis/identities/initialize_identities.py','spatial-gev/adapters/grizos_projection_gateway.py','spatial-gev/deploy/deploy_gev.sh','apple-clients/discovery/discover_xcode.py','operations/field_start.py','operations/field_status.py','operations/field_stop.py','acceptance/production_acceptance.py','acceptance/restart_recovery.py','SOURCE_MATERIAL/SOURCE_HASHES.json','REPO_OBSERVATIONS.json']
for r in required:
    f=root/r
    if not f.exists() or (f.is_file() and f.stat().st_size<40): err.append('missing/substantive '+r)
for f in root.rglob('*'):
    if f.is_symlink():
        t=str(f.resolve()).lower()
        if 'gmri_overnight_drop' in t or 'gmri-overnight-integration-plan.md' in t: err.append('prohibited symlink '+str(f))
acc=(root/'acceptance/production_acceptance.py').read_text().lower()
for term in ['fixture','mock','counter','testdata']:
    if term not in acc: err.append('acceptance missing synthetic guard '+term)
start=(root/'START_HERE.md').read_text().lower(); topo=(root/'PRODUCTION_TOPOLOGY.md').read_text().lower()
if 'operator lane' not in start or 'observer lane' not in start: err.append('two-lane proxmox missing')
if 'gmri-core' not in topo or 'gmri-gev' not in topo: err.append('logical production resources missing')
for f in root.rglob('*.json'):
    try: json.loads(f.read_text())
    except Exception as e: err.append(f'json {f.relative_to(root)}: {e}')
for f in root.rglob('*.py'):
    try: compile(f.read_text(),str(f),'exec')
    except Exception as e: err.append(f'python syntax {f.relative_to(root)}: {e}')
for f in root.rglob('*.sh'):
    r=subprocess.run(['bash','-n',str(f)],capture_output=True,text=True)
    if r.returncode: err.append(f'shell syntax {f.relative_to(root)}: {r.stderr.strip()}')
# Source provenance must only name the clean source whitelist/current mission for copied files.
prov=root/'BUILD_PROVENANCE.json'
if prov.exists():
    try:
        pr=json.loads(prov.read_text())
        for rel,row in pr.items():
            sp=str(row.get('source_path','')).lower()
            if 'gmri_overnight_drop' in sp or 'gmri-overnight-integration-plan.md' in sp: err.append('prohibited provenance '+rel)
    except Exception as e: err.append('provenance parse '+str(e))
if err:
    print('PACKET_VALIDATION_FAIL')
    for e in err: print('-',e)
    raise SystemExit(2)
print('PACKET_VALIDATION_PASS')
print('files='+str(sum(1 for f in root.rglob('*') if f.is_file())))
''', True)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
import argparse,json
from pathlib import Path
p=argparse.ArgumentParser(); p.add_argument('--inventory',required=True); p.add_argument('--desired',default=str(Path(__file__).with_name('desired_resources.json'))); p.add_argument('--policy',required=True); p.add_argument('--out',required=True); a=p.parse_args()

# Policy values must name resources that actually exist in the observer inventory. OMP derives policy from live known-good state/current network intent; resolver never picks a first item.
def getname(x,*keys):
    for k in keys:
        if x.get(k) is not None: return str(x[k])
def select(rows,wanted,keys,label):
    hit=[x for x in rows if getname(x,*keys)==str(wanted)]
    if len(hit)!=1: raise SystemExit(f'BLOCKED_REQUIRES_OPERATOR: selected {label} {wanted!r} not uniquely present in observer inventory')
    return hit[0]
node_row=select(inv['nodes'],pol.get('node'),('node','name'),'node'); node=getname(node_row,'node','name')
st_row=select(inv['storages'],pol.get('storage'),('storage','name'),'storage'); storage=getname(st_row,'storage','name')
net_row=select(inv['networks'],pol.get('bridge'),('bridge','name'),'bridge'); bridge=getname(net_row,'bridge','name')
if st_row.get('active') is False: raise SystemExit('BLOCKED_REQUIRES_OPERATOR: selected storage is not active')
used=set()
for g in inv.get('guests',[]):
    for k in ('vmid','id'):
        try: used.add(int(g[k])); break
        except Exception: pass
nextid=int(pol.get('vmid_floor',100))
while nextid in used: nextid+=1
resolved=[]
for r in des['resources']:
    existing=next((g for g in inv.get('guests',[]) if g.get('name')==r['logical_name'] and g.get('gmri_canonical') is True),None)
    if existing:
        resolved.append({'logical_name':r['logical_name'],'action':'ADOPT_VERIFY','existing':existing,'node':existing.get('node',node),'evidence_required':'existing resource must pass production service standard before adoption'})
    else:
        while nextid in used: nextid+=1
        resolved.append({'logical_name':r['logical_name'],'action':'CREATE','vmid':nextid,'node':node,'storage':storage,'bridge':bridge,'requested':r['requested'],'network_policy':r['network'],'rollback_required_before_mutation':True})
        used.add(nextid); nextid+=1
out={'source_inventory':a.inventory,'selection_policy':a.policy,'resolved':resolved,'status':'RESOLVED_FROM_OBSERVED_INVENTORY_AND_EXPLICIT_LIVE_POLICY'}
